rules.title: What counts as 'public works'
rules.plain_english: Construction, alteration, demolition, installation or repair work done under contract and paid for in whole or in part with public funds is a public work, so prevailing wage law applies.

elements: paid in whole or part out of public funds
also_covers: street, sewer or other improvement work under public authority
tree removal in execution of a covered project
excludes: work done directly by a public utility company under PUC order

rules.applies_to: Any contractor or subcontractor working on publicly funded projects in California
rules.verbatim_quote: As used in this chapter, “public works” means all of the following: (1) Construction, alteration, demolition, installation, or repair work done under contract and paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, except work done directly by a public utility company pursuant to order of the Public Utilities Commission or other public authority.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Also see DIR summary at https://www.dir.ca.gov/Public-Works/PublicWorks.html (maintenance is also covered per LC 1771).

rules.title: Pre- and post-construction work is 'construction'
rules.plain_english: Design-phase site assessment, feasibility, inspection and land surveying work, and post-construction cleanup at the jobsite count as covered 'construction', even if no further construction happens.

parameters.installation_includes: assembly/disassembly of freestanding and affixed modular office systems

rules.applies_to: Surveyors, inspectors, cleanup crews and other pre/post-construction workers on public projects
rules.verbatim_quote: “construction” includes work performed during the design, site assessment, feasibility study, and other preconstruction phases of construction, including, but not limited to, inspection and land surveying work, regardless of whether any further construction work is conducted, and work performed during the postconstruction phases of construction, including, but not limited to
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: 'Paid for out of public funds' includes indirect subsidies
rules.plain_english: A project is publicly funded not only when a public agency pays cash, but also when it does construction work, transfers property below market value, waives or reduces fees, rents, loans or interest, makes contingent loans, or gives credits.

forms: payment of money or equivalent to or on behalf of contractor/developer
construction work performed by the public entity
transfer of asset for less than fair market price
fees/costs/rents/insurance/bond premiums/loans/interest paid, reduced, below market, waived or forgiven
money loaned repayable on a contingent basis

rules.applies_to: Developers and contractors on private projects that receive public assistance
rules.verbatim_quote: (3) Transfer by the state or political subdivision of an asset of value for less than fair market price. (4) Fees, costs, rents, insurance or bond premiums, loans, interest rates, or other obligations that would normally be required in the execution of the contract, that are paid, reduced, charged at less than fair market value, waived, or forgiven by the state or political subdivision.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. If a project is later found to be public work, see rule pw-1784-recover-increased-costs.

rules.title: De minimis public subsidy exception ($600,000 and 2%)
rules.plain_english: A private development does not become a public work because of a small public subsidy: the subsidy must be both under $600,000 and under 2% of total project cost (for all-single-family projects, only the under-2% test applies).
rules.applies_to: Private developers and their contractors receiving public subsidies
rules.verbatim_quote: For purposes of subparagraph (A), a public subsidy is de minimis if it is both less than six hundred thousand dollars ($600,000) and less than 2 percent of the total project cost. (ii) Notwithstanding clause (i), for purposes of subparagraph (A), a public subsidy for a project that consists entirely of single-family dwellings is de minimis if it is less than 2 percent of the total project cost.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Subdivision (c)(3)(A) also excludes reimbursement of costs normally borne by the public.

rules.title: Private residential projects on private property excluded
rules.plain_english: Private residential projects built on private property are not public works unless built under an agreement with a state agency, redevelopment agency (or successor), or local public housing authority.

parameters.excluded: private residential projects on private property

rules.verbatim_quote: (1) Private residential projects built on private property are not subject to this chapter unless the projects are built pursuant to an agreement with a state agency, a redevelopment agency, a successor agency to a redevelopment agency when acting in that capacity, or a local public housing authority.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Other residential exclusions in 1720(c)(5) (self-help housing with >=500 buyer hours, homeless shelters, etc.) and 1720(d).

rules.title: Definition of 'maintenance' (lower $15,000 small-project threshold)
rules.plain_english: Maintenance means routine, recurring work to keep a public facility in safe, usable condition, including craft repair work; routine janitorial and security guard services are not covered maintenance.

includes: routine, recurring and usual preservation work on publicly owned/operated facilities
carpentry, electrical, plumbing, glazing, touchup painting and other craft work

rules.verbatim_quote: (1) Routine, recurring and usual work for the preservation, protection and keeping of any publicly owned or publicly operated facility (plant, building, structure, ground facility, utility system or any real property) for its intended purposes in a safe and continually usable condition for which it has been designed, improved, constructed, altered or repaired.
rules.notes: Used to decide whether the $15,000 (maintenance) or $25,000 (construction) small-project threshold applies.

rules.title: Prevailing wage required on public works over $1,000
rules.plain_english: Every worker on a public works project over $1,000 must be paid at least the prevailing wage, including holiday and overtime rates. It applies to maintenance contracts, but not to a public agency's own employees.
rules.verbatim_quote: Except for public works projects of one thousand dollars ($1,000) or less, not less than the general prevailing rate of per diem wages for work of a similar character in the locality in which the public work is performed, and not less than the general prevailing rate of per diem wages for holiday and overtime work fixed as provided in this chapter
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. DIR FAQ notes some LCP-enforcing awarding bodies historically had higher exemption thresholds ($25,000/$15,000) under LC 1771.5.

rules.title: No splitting projects to dodge thresholds
rules.plain_english: Jobs may not be split or parceled into smaller work orders to get under the $1,000 prevailing wage threshold or the $25,000/$15,000 small-project thresholds. If yearly work with the same vendor will exceed the threshold, the vendor must register and the contract must be registered.
rules.applies_to: Awarding bodies and contractors on recurring/small public jobs
rules.verbatim_quote: Prevailing wage requirements apply to public works projects over $1,000. The law does not permit jobs to be parceled in order to avoid the $1,000 threshold. If the awarding body knows that total yearly project costs or projects awarded to the same vendor will exceed $1,000, that vendor must be registered with the DIR as a public works contractor
rules.notes: 8 CCR 16100(b)(6): awarding body must 'Ensure that public works projects are not split or separated into smaller work orders or projects for the purpose of evading the applicable provisions of Labor Code Section 1771.'

rules.title: Prime and every subcontractor must pay prevailing rates to all workers
rules.plain_english: The prime contractor and every subcontractor must pay at least the specified prevailing rates to every worker employed in executing the contract, regardless of the worker's title (owner, partner, foreman, independent contractor).

parameters.who_is_covered: all workers employed in the execution of the contract

rules.source_location: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf PDF page 977 (Appendix, Labor Code §1774); PDF page 967 (§1772)
rules.verbatim_quote: The contractor to whom the contract is awarded, and any subcontractor under him, shall pay not less than the specified prevailing rates of wages to all workmen employed in the execution of the contract.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. LC 1772: workers employed by contractors or subcontractors in the execution of any contract for public work are deemed employed upon public work.

rules.title: Sole proprietors/owner-operators must earn at least the prevailing wage
rules.plain_english: An owner who does the work must show that the labor portion of the contract (contract price minus materials, overhead and other costs, divided by hours worked) is at least the prevailing rate, and must still submit eCPRs. Salaried corporate officers doing covered work are annualized and topped up if below the rate.

parameters.corporate_officer_salary: annualize to hourly; pay difference if below prevailing rate

rules.applies_to: Sole proprietors, partners and owner-operators doing covered work
rules.verbatim_quote: Divide profit before labor costs (the amount of the contract, less fixed and variable costs) by the total number of hours worked on the public works site. If labor profit falls below the prevailing wage rate, the contractor could be subject to public works penalties for failing to pay the correct prevailing wage rate.
rules.notes: Use SSN or ITIN when reporting if no FEIN. Owners cannot underbid labor cost.

rules.title: Ask DIR for a coverage determination when unsure
rules.plain_english: If you are unsure whether a job is a public work, the awarding body or any interested party (contractor, union, worker) can request a written coverage determination from DIR's Director.

parameters.request_to: pwcoverage@dir.ca.gov (DIR Office of the Director, Legal Unit)

rules.applies_to: Contractors and owners on projects with public money
rules.verbatim_quote: If you need assistance determining whether a project constitutes a public work, you may request a coverage determination with the DIR Office of the Director, Legal Unit, at pwcoverage@dir.ca.gov.
rules.notes: Past determinations: https://www.dir.ca.gov/oprl/PWDecision.asp

rules.title: Recovering prevailing wage costs when a private job is later ruled public work
rules.plain_english: If a private job is later ruled a public work and nobody told you it was, you can sue your hiring party for the extra wages and penalties, but you must notify the hiring party and owner/developer within 30 days of the DIR/LWDA decision or court filing, by registered/certified mail, express mail or overnight carrier.

parameters.trigger: receipt of DIR/LWDA decision or initiation of court action alleging public work
not_available_if: owner/hiring party expressly advised it was public work

rules.applies_to: CSLB-licensed contractors with a direct contract on a private project later deemed public work
rules.verbatim_quote: the contractor shall notify the hiring party and the owner or developer within 30 days after receipt of the notice of a decision by the Department of Industrial Relations or the Labor and Workforce Development Agency, or the initiation of any action in a court alleging, that the work covered by the project, or any portion thereof, is a “public work,” as defined in this chapter.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Also (c): such violations need not be listed on prequalification questionnaires.

rules.title: DIR public works contractor registration required
rules.plain_english: A contractor or subcontractor cannot bid, be listed in a bid, or work on a public works contract unless currently registered with DIR under Labor Code 1725.5 (unless the small-project exemption applies).

required_for: being listed as a subcontractor in a bid

rules.applies_to: All prime contractors and subcontractors (any tier) on public works
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) A contractor or subcontractor shall not be qualified to bid on, be listed in a bid proposal, subject to the requirements of Section 4104 of the Public Contract Code, or engage in the performance of any contract for public work, as defined in this chapter, unless currently registered and qualified to perform public work pursuant to Section 1725.5.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Per FindLaw snippets a new version of LC 1725.5 became operative July 1, 2026 (with interim LC 1725.6 sunsetting); text not read. rules.title: Who must register (separate licenses, joint employers, sole proprietors)
rules.plain_english: Each separately licensed business entity, every independent contractor doing prevailing wage work, joint employers such as temp staffing agencies and labor contractors, brokers who sub out the actual work, and owner-operator sole proprietors must each register.

must_register: each separately CSLB-licensed entity/name bidding or working on public works
independent contractors performing prevailing wage work
joint employers incl. temp staffing agencies, PEOs, labor contractors
entities that contract and then subcontract all the actual work
parameters.employee_test: not an employee of a registered contractor unless that contractor carries workers' comp for the person

rules.verbatim_quote: (1) Each business entity or name that is separately licensed by the Contractors State License Board or other licensing entity and intends to bid or work on public works through that separate license, irrespective of whether the separately licensed entities or business names share a common ownership.
rules.notes: DIR FAQ: registration not required for projects under complete control of the federal government (Davis-Bacon only).

rules.title: Registration fee: $400 per fiscal year (1-3 years)
rules.plain_english: Registration or renewal costs $400 per fiscal year; you can register for one, two or three years at once ($400, $800 or $1,200). Fees are nonrefundable and registration is not complete until payment is processed.
rules.applies_to: All public works contractors and subcontractors
rules.verbatim_quote: (6) The fees specified in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) are for registration or renewal for a single fiscal year, as determined in accordance with section 16410(b). A contractor or subcontractor may apply to register or renew for one, two, or three years by paying the fee specified in paragraphs (1), (2), or (3) for each year of registration or renewal
rules.notes: CSLB Summer 2026 newsletter also states $400 per fiscal year. SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1741, 1775, 1776, 1777.7 and 1813 to raise penalties/fees; final amounts and operative date NOT verified (bill analyses only) - re-check before 2027. (SB 909 analyses describe letting the DIR Director set/CPI-adjust the fee.)

rules.title: Registration runs July 1 - June 30; renew by June 30
rules.plain_english: Registration covers the July 1 to June 30 fiscal year (or the remainder of it), no matter when you register. Renew before June 30 to avoid penalties.
rules.verbatim_quote: (b) All registrations shall be for the July 1 to June 30 fiscal year or any part of the fiscal year that remains following the date of registration.
rules.notes: dir.ca.gov/pw: 'Your registration must be valid each year by June 30 to prevent penalties.'

rules.title: $2,000 penalty to register after working/bidding unregistered
rules.plain_english: If you worked on, bid on, or were listed on a bid for a public works project in the past 12 months while unregistered, you must pay an extra $2,000 penalty (plus the $400 fee) to register. For a single violation in 12 months you can still register by paying it.
rules.applies_to: Contractors registering for the first time or reactivating
rules.verbatim_quote: (4) Additional penalty to apply for registration if contractor or subcontractor has worked, bid, or been listed on a bid in violation of the requirements of Labor Code Section 1725.5(a) within the preceding twelve months - $2000
rules.notes: DIR may refund the penalty on clear and convincing proof it did not apply (16412(d)). SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1741, 1775, 1776, 1777.7 and 1813 to raise penalties/fees; final amounts and operative date NOT verified (bill analyses only) - re-check before 2027.

rules.title: Late renewal: 90-day grace with $400 penalty
rules.plain_english: If your registration lapses and you keep working or bidding, you can renew retroactively within 90 days after expiration (July 1 - Sept 30) by paying a $400 penalty plus the renewal fee if the lapse was accidental ($2,000 if not accidental). Renewing after September 30 (or reactivating) costs a $2,000 penalty if you bid, were awarded or worked on public works while unregistered in the past 12 months.
rules.applies_to: Registered contractors who miss the June 30 renewal
rules.citation: 8 CCR 16412(a)(5); DIR FAQ; DIR registration page
rules.verbatim_quote: Registered contractors who inadvertently fail to renew by June 30, but continue to work on public works after that date, have a 90-day grace period to renew retroactively by paying a $400 penalty in addition to the registration renewal fee.
rules.notes: Accidental vs. non-accidental split ($400 vs $2,000) is from DIR registration page dated April 2026. 8 CCR 16412(a)(5) text: '$400' during first ninety days for inadvertent lapse.

rules.title: Registration eligibility requirements
rules.plain_english: To register you must: carry workers' comp for any employees and use only registered subcontractors; hold a CSLB license if your trade requires one; owe no delinquent unpaid wage or penalty assessments; not be debarred; and not have prior registration violations (first violation in 12 months can be cured with the penalty).

requirements: no prior registration violation (first in 12 months curable by penalty)

rules.verbatim_quote: Have workers' compensation coverage for any employees and only use subcontractors who are registered public works contractors. Have Contractors State License Board license if applicable to trade. Not have any delinquent unpaid wage or penalty assessments owed to any employee or enforcement agency. Not be under federal or state debarment.
rules.notes: Workers' comp evidence (per secondary snippets of LC 1725.5): certificate of insurance or self-insurance under B&P 7125.

rules.title: Pay by credit card: registration posts in about 24 hours
rules.plain_english: Credit card registrations are processed within about 24 hours; other payment methods can delay registration up to eight weeks. Plan ahead of bid dates.
rules.verbatim_quote: Please note: credit card payments can be processed within 24 hours while other forms of payment may delay registration up to eight weeks.
rules.notes: Since May 24, 2024 contractors must create accounts on the modernized Public Works Website Services.

rules.title: Two registration violations in 12 months: up to 12 months disqualification
rules.plain_english: Contractors found violating the registration requirement twice within 12 months can be barred from public works for up to 12 months at a time.
rules.verbatim_quote: Contractors who are found to be in violation of the registration requirement twice in 12 months can be disqualified from working in public works for up to 12 months at a time.

rules.title: Appeal of registration denial within 60 days
rules.plain_english: If DIR denies your registration on the merits, you can appeal in writing within 60 days; a hearing is set within 30 days of the appeal.
rules.verbatim_quote: (c) Within sixty (60) days following the issuance of any notice of denial pursuant to subsection (b), including a notification of denial provided at the conclusion of the online registration process or any written notice of denial that is subsequently transmitted, mailed, or delivered to the applicant for registration
rules.notes: Denial for incomplete application is without prejudice to reapplying (16413(a)).

rules.title: Registration revocation: 10 days to stay, 60 days to appeal; 30 days-24 months disqualification
rules.plain_english: DIR can revoke registration (e.g., no longer qualified, false certification, or knowingly hiring unregistered subs). Revocation takes effect at 11:59 p.m. on the 10th day after notice unless you appeal within those 10 days; you may still appeal up to 60 days, but a late appeal does not stop the revocation. Disqualification is 30 days to 24 months.
rules.verbatim_quote: (d) Except as provided in section 16417, revocation shall be effective at 11:59 p.m. on the tenth day following the date the Labor Commissioner sends the written notice of revocation specified in subsections (b) and (c), unless prior to that deadline the Department receives the contractor or subcontractor's written appeal under subsection (e).
rules.notes: 16414(b): 'The period of disqualification shall be no less than 30 days and no greater than 24 months following the effective date of revocation.' Decision within 5 days (stayed) or 10 days of hearing; writ within 45 days (16416).

rules.title: Working unregistered: $100/day up to $8,000
rules.plain_english: A contractor or subcontractor who works on a public works contract without registration owes $100 for each day of work, up to $8,000, on top of the $2,000 registration penalty fee.
rules.verbatim_quote: shall forfeit, as a civil penalty to the state, one hundred dollars ($100) for each day of work performed in violation of the registration requirement, not to exceed an aggregate penalty of eight thousand dollars ($8,000) in addition to any penalty registration fee assessed pursuant to clause (ii) of subparagraph (E) of paragraph (2) of subdivision (a) of Section 1725.5.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1741, 1775, 1776, 1777.7 and 1813 to raise penalties/fees; final amounts and operative date NOT verified (bill analyses only) - re-check before 2027.

rules.title: Hiring an unregistered sub: $100/day up to $10,000; no indemnity
rules.plain_english: A prime or higher-tier sub that subcontracts with an unregistered lower-tier sub owes $100 for each day the unregistered sub works, up to $10,000. You cannot make the sub indemnify you for this penalty. No liability if the sub's registration was later revoked; first-time unintentional violations may be waived.

parameters.waivable: first-time, unintentional, did not hinder enforcement

rules.verbatim_quote: shall be subject to forfeiture, as a civil penalty to the state, of one hundred dollars ($100) for each day the unregistered lower tier subcontractor performs work in violation of the registration requirement, not to exceed an aggregate penalty of ten thousand dollars ($10,000).
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Check sub registration at https://services.dir.ca.gov/pw before signing subcontracts.

rules.title: Stop order against unregistered contractors; idled workers paid up to 10 days
rules.plain_english: The Labor Commissioner must issue a stop order barring an unregistered contractor from all public works until it registers. Workers idled by the stop order must be paid their regular prevailing rate for up to 10 days.
rules.applies_to: Unregistered contractors and those who hire them
rules.verbatim_quote: (4) Any employee of an unregistered contractor or subcontractor who is affected by a work stoppage ordered by the commissioner pursuant to this subdivision shall be paid at his or her regular hourly prevailing wage rate by that employer for any hours the employee would have worked but for the work stoppage, not to exceed 10 days.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Ignoring a stop order: misdemeanor, up to 60 days jail / $10,000
rules.plain_english: A contractor, owner, director, officer or managing agent who fails to observe a served stop order is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by up to 60 days in county jail, a fine up to $10,000, or both.
rules.applies_to: Unregistered contractors served with stop orders
rules.verbatim_quote: (k) Failure of a contractor or subcontractor, owner, director, officer, or managing agent of the contractor or subcontractor to observe a stop order issued and served upon him or her pursuant to subdivision (j) is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment in county jail not exceeding 60 days or by a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000), or both.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Inadvertently listing an unregistered sub: cure options
rules.plain_english: Listing an unregistered subcontractor by mistake does not make the bid nonresponsive if the sub registered before bid opening, registers and pays the penalty fee within 24 hours after bid opening, or is replaced with a registered sub under PCC 4107.

cure_options: sub registers and pays penalty fee within 24 hours after bid opening

rules.verbatim_quote: (c) An inadvertent error in listing a subcontractor who is not registered pursuant to Section 1725.5 in a bid proposal shall not be grounds for filing a bid protest or grounds for considering the bid nonresponsive, provided that any of the following apply: (1) The subcontractor is registered prior to the bid opening. (2) Within 24 hours after the bid opening
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Proof of registration before accepting bids or signing subcontracts
rules.plain_english: Bid invitations and public works contracts must give notice of the registration requirement, and no bid may be accepted and no contract or subcontract signed without proof of the contractor's or subcontractor's current DIR registration.
rules.verbatim_quote: (b) Notice of the requirement described in subdivision (a) shall be included in all bid invitations and public works contracts, and a bid shall not be accepted nor any contract or subcontract entered into without proof of the contractor or subcontractor’s current registration to perform public work pursuant to Section 1725.5.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. A tool can verify PWCR numbers against DIR's public contractor search before subcontract execution.

rules.title: Small project exemption: $25,000 construction / $15,000 maintenance
rules.plain_english: On public works of $25,000 or less (construction, alteration, demolition, installation or repair) or $15,000 or less (maintenance), contractors need not register with DIR or file eCPRs, and the awarding body need not file the PWC-100. Prevailing wages (over $1,000) and certified payroll records still apply; keep the records at least 3 years.
rules.applies_to: Contractors working exclusively on small public works projects
rules.source_location: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf PDF page 958 (Appendix, Labor Code §1771.1(n)); PDF page 961 (§1771.4(a)(4))
rules.verbatim_quote: (n) This section shall not apply to work performed on a public works project of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) or less when the project is for construction, alteration, demolition, installation, or repair work or to work performed on a public works project of fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000) or less when the project is for maintenance work.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. LC 1771.4(a)(4): unregistered small-project contractors 'shall retain the records specified in Section 1776 for at least three years after completion of the work.'

rules.title: Small-project exemption is measured on the whole prime contract
rules.plain_english: The $25,000/$15,000 test uses the entire contract between the awarding body and the prime contractor, not the size of your subcontract. A $10,000 subcontract on a $500,000 job is not exempt.

parameters.measure: awarding body to prime contractor contract amount

rules.verbatim_quote: Keep in mind that this amount is for the entire contract between the Awarding Body and the Prime Contractor. If the subcontract is less than this amount but the master contract is more than this amount then it would not fall under the small project exemption.

rules.title: Joint venture and federal-aid bids: register by contract award
rules.plain_english: An unregistered contractor may submit a joint-venture bid (B&P 7029.1) or a bid on a federally funded project (PCC 10164/20103.5) as long as it is registered when the contract is awarded.
rules.applies_to: Joint ventures and bidders on federally funded projects
rules.verbatim_quote: It is not a violation of this section for an unregistered contractor to submit a bid that is authorized by Section 7029.1 of the Business and Professions Code or by Section 10164 or 20103.5 of the Public Contract Code, provided the contractor is registered to perform public work pursuant to Section 1725.5 at the time the contract is awarded.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Awarding body must register project (PWC-100) within 30 days of award
rules.plain_english: The awarding body must electronically notify DIR of each public works contract within 30 days after award and no later than the first day any contractor has workers on the job. Contractors cannot file eCPRs until the project is registered.

parameters.latest: first day contractor has workers employed
parameters.jobs_under_PCC_10122_20113_20654_22050: within 30 days after award but no later than last day workers employed

rules.applies_to: Awarding bodies; contractors should confirm project is registered
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) (1) An awarding body shall provide notice to the Department of Industrial Relations of any public works contract subject to the requirements of this chapter, within 30 days of the award, but in no event later than the first day in which a contractor has workers employed upon the public work.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Development proponents (Gov. Code 65852.24, 65912.130, 65913.4) also register projects with DIR.

rules.title: Project registration contents
rules.plain_english: The DIR project notice must include the prime contractor's and listed subcontractors' names and DIR registration numbers, bid and award dates, contract amount, estimated start and completion dates and jobsite location.

parameters.format: electronic via DIR Public Works Website Services

rules.verbatim_quote: (3) The notice shall be transmitted electronically in a format specified by the department and shall include the name and registration number issued by the Department of Industrial Relations pursuant to Section 1725.5 of the contractor, the name and registration number issued by the Department of Industrial Relations pursuant to Section 1725.5 of any subcontractor listed on the successful bid
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Unlisted subs can request to join the project in the DIR portal (DIR FAQ).

rules.title: Awarding body penalty: $100/day up to $10,000 per project; contractors cannot be charged
rules.plain_english: An awarding body that fails to register the project, or contracts with/permits an unregistered contractor, faces $100 per day up to $10,000 per project. Contractors are not liable for these penalties and cannot be required to indemnify the awarding body.
rules.applies_to: Awarding bodies; contract reviewers (reject indemnity clauses)
rules.verbatim_quote: (h) A contractor or subcontractor shall not be liable for any penalties assessed against an awarding body pursuant to this section. An awarding body may not require a contractor or subcontractor to indemnify or otherwise be liable for any penalties assessed against an awarding body pursuant to this section.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Two or more willful violations in 12 months: awarding body loses state construction funding for one year (1773.3(g)).

rules.title: Final payment withheld until 30 days after full subcontractor list submitted
rules.plain_english: The awarding body must hold the prime's final payment until at least 30 days after all required project information, including a complete subcontractor list, has been submitted to DIR. Paying early and later finding an unregistered sub exposes it to $100/day up to 100 days per unregistered contractor.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (final payment timing) and awarding bodies
rules.verbatim_quote: (d) An awarding body shall withhold final payment due to the contractor until at least 30 days after all of the required information in paragraph (2) of subdivision (a) has been submitted, including, but not limited to, providing a complete list of all subcontractors.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Cash-flow planning: final payment cannot be expected sooner than 30 days after a complete sub list is in DIR's system.

rules.title: Bid and contract documents must state DIR compliance monitoring
rules.plain_english: Calls for bids and contract documents must state that the project is subject to compliance monitoring and enforcement by DIR.

parameters.required_statement: project is subject to compliance monitoring and enforcement by the Department of Industrial Relations

rules.verbatim_quote: (1) The call for bids and contract documents shall specify that the project is subject to compliance monitoring and enforcement by the Department of Industrial Relations.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Applies to contracts awarded on or after Jan. 1, 2015 (1771.4(c)).

rules.title: Required public works job site postings
rules.plain_english: Each job site must have posted: the Director's prevailing wage determinations for the crafts on the job (one location OK if multiple sites), the DIR compliance monitoring notice, and the payday notice (Labor Code 207). The awarding body posts or requires the prime to post.

postings: DIR prevailing wage rate determination(s) for each craft
DIR/DLSE compliance monitoring (CMU) notice per 8 CCR 16451(d)
notice of paydays and time/place of payment (LC 207)
parameters.who_posts: awarding body or prime contractor if required
parameters.multiple_worksites: may post at one location readily available to all workers

rules.verbatim_quote: “This public works project is subject to monitoring and investigative activities by the Compliance Monitoring Unit (CMU) of the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement, Department of Industrial Relations, State of California. This Notice is intended to provide information to all workers employed in the execution of the contract for public work
rules.notes: Full CMU notice text (including blank for local DLSE office phone) is in 8 CCR 16451(d) - a tool can generate it verbatim. LC 1773.2: awarding body 'shall also cause a copy of the determination of the director of the prevailing rate of per diem wages to be posted at each job site.'

rules.title: Prevailing rates must be in (or referenced by) the bid call and contract
rules.plain_english: The awarding body must state the prevailing per diem wage rates for each craft in the call for bids, bid specifications and contract, or state that copies are on file at its principal office and available on request.

parameters.alternative: statement that rates are on file at principal office and available on request

rules.applies_to: Awarding bodies; primes flowing down to subs
rules.verbatim_quote: The body awarding any contract for public work, or otherwise undertaking any public work, shall specify in the call for bids for the contract, and in the bid specifications and in the contract itself, what the general rate of per diem wages is for each craft, classification, or type of worker needed to execute the contract.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Electronic certified payroll (eCPR) to DIR at least every 30 days
rules.plain_english: Every contractor and subcontractor must upload certified payroll records directly to the Labor Commissioner through DIR's portal at least once every 30 days while working, and within 30 days after the last day of work (or more often if the contract says so). Best practice is weekly.

parameters.format: online form or XML upload (V2 schema)

rules.applies_to: All contractors/subcontractors on non-exempt public works
rules.verbatim_quote: (i) At least monthly or more frequently if specified in the contract with the awarding body. For purposes of this clause, “monthly” means that a submission of records shall be made at least once every 30 days while work is being performed on the project and within 30 days after the final day of work performed on the project.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Applies to all contracts, new or ongoing, on or after Jan. 1, 2016 (1771.4(d)).

rules.title: Late eCPRs: $100/day up to $5,000 per project (after 14-day grace)
rules.plain_english: A contractor that fails to submit eCPRs is subject to $100 per day of violation, up to $5,000 per project. The penalty cannot be levied until the records are 14 days past due, and only the contractor that failed to file is liable.

parameters.liable_party: only the contractor/subcontractor that failed to furnish

rules.verbatim_quote: (C) The Labor Commissioner shall not levy a penalty pursuant to subparagraph (B) until a contractor or subcontractor fails to furnish the records pursuant to subparagraph (A) 14 days after the requirement set forth in clause (i) of subparagraph (A).
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. 14-day grace added by AB 1023 (Stats 2021 ch 326), effective 1/1/2022. Penalty amount per (B): 'one hundred dollars ($100) per each day ... not to exceed a total penalty of five thousand dollars ($5,000) per project.'

rules.title: eCPR exemptions: legacy LCPs and qualifying PLAs only
rules.plain_english: Only projects monitored by the four legacy labor compliance programs (Caltrans, City of Los Angeles, LAUSD, County of Sacramento) or covered by a qualifying project labor agreement with a wage dispute mechanism, plus small projects, are exempt from filing eCPRs with DIR.

parameters.exempt_pla: awarding body CBA binding all contractors with wage dispute mechanism

rules.applies_to: Contractors deciding whether eCPRs are needed
rules.citation: Labor Code 1771.4(b); DIR eCPR exemptions page
rules.verbatim_quote: Only projects monitored and enforced by an approved labor compliance program (LCP) or covered by a qualifying project labor agreement may be exempted from the requirement to submit certified payroll records to DIR.
rules.notes: Exempt contractors still keep CPRs and produce them on request (LC 1776).

rules.title: Sending CPRs to the prime, union, awarding body or LCP does not replace eCPR
rules.plain_english: Each company must submit its own eCPRs directly to DIR; giving payrolls to the prime contractor, a union, the awarding body or an LCP does not satisfy the DIR requirement.
rules.verbatim_quote: Yes. Submitting certified payroll records to other agencies does not fulfill the requirement to submit certified payroll records to the Labor Commissioner/DIR.
rules.notes: Prop 84 projects: submit to both DIR and the LCP (DIR FAQ).

rules.title: eCPR filing does not excuse answering a written CPR request (and vice versa)
rules.plain_english: Uploading eCPRs is a separate duty from responding within 10 days to a written request for certified payroll records under LC 1776; eCPRs lack some required A-1-131 information (gross weekly earnings, itemized deductions, etc.).

separate_duties: certified copies on written request within 10 days (LC 1776(d))
parameters.form_for_requests: DIR Form A-1-131 or equivalent with all LC 1776 info

rules.verbatim_quote: Thus, a contractor that has electronically furnished eCPRs is not excused from timely furnishing to the Labor Commissioner “a certified copy of all payroll records” within 10 days after receipt of such a written request.
rules.notes: Public Works Manual is an official Labor Commissioner training publication, not binding law.

rules.title: Mark the final eCPR; file Statements of Non-Performance for weeks with no work
rules.plain_english: When filing the last eCPR for a job, answer 'Yes' to the final eCPR question. For payroll weeks with no work, submit a Statement of Non-Performance (statementOfNP=true). Submitted records cannot be deleted; correct them by submitting an amended record for the same period, which takes precedence.

parameters.amendments: new record for same period supersedes; original stays visible

rules.citation: Labor Code 1771.4; DIR FAQ; eCPR XML Guidelines V2 §5.4-5.5
rules.source_location: https://www.dir.ca.gov/Public-Works/PublicWorksSB854FAQ.html (Viewing, Correcting, and Amending Records; Completing the Payroll Information Fields); https://www.dir.ca.gov/Public-Works/CPR/eCPR-XML-Guidelines-V2.pdf
rules.verbatim_quote: Yes. When submitting the final eCPR for a job, select Yes on the submission form’s final eCPR question.
rules.notes: FAQ: 'You cannot change or delete payroll records that have already been submitted (except for non-performance submissions). However, you may correct errors by submitting a new record for the same pay period.'

rules.title: How to report fringes, deductions and mixed public/private pay on eCPRs
rules.plain_english: Report the pre-tax hourly rate. Fringes paid directly to the worker go into the hourly rate; fringes paid to a fund are reported as hourly contribution rates (same for ST/OT/DT). Deductions and payments (e.g., travel/subsistence) are reported as period totals; enter 0 in required fields with no withholding. If a check covers public and private work, report this-project gross and all-work gross.

parameters.fringe_paid_to_plan: report as hourly contribution per classification

rules.citation: DIR FAQ (Completing the Payroll Information Fields)
rules.verbatim_quote: Whether fringe benefits are included in the hourly rate depends on how they are paid to employees. If paid directly to the worker, include them in the hourly rate. If paid into a fund or to a committee, do not include them in the hourly rate. Indicate them in the contribution section instead.
rules.notes: Notes field is publicly visible - no personal information.

rules.title: eCPR XML V2: PWCR number (10 digits) and DIR project ID are mandatory
rules.plain_english: Every eCPR XML file must carry the contractor's 10-digit PWCR registration number and the numeric DIR project ID exactly as on file; a mismatch is a hard failure. The version element must be 2.0; payrollNum and amendmentNum are left empty.
rules.citation: Labor Code 1771.4(a)(3)(A)(ii); DIR eCPR XML Guidelines V2 (Nov. 2026)
rules.verbatim_quote: contractorPWCR is now required and must be exactly 10 numeric digits, matching the PWCR number on file with DIR. The option to enter “NA” has been removed.
rules.notes: Element order must match the XSD exactly or validation fails.

rules.title: eCPR XML V2: weekly structure and hour limits
rules.plain_english: Each payroll week ends on forWeekEnding and covers that date plus the six prior days. Each classification needs exactly seven day elements (id 1-7, id 7 = week-ending date), hours >=0 and <100 with two decimals, and an employee's ST+OT+DT across all classifications may not exceed 24 hours in a day. totHrs must equal the daily sums.
rules.verbatim_quote: Each classification must include exactly seven-day elements, one for each day of the payroll week, even if the employee did not work on a given day.

rules.title: eCPR XML V2: preparer-calculated totals (not recalculated by DIR)
rules.plain_english: Total hourly rates must equal the base ST/OT/DT rate plus the sum of fringe amounts for that classification; totalDeductions must equal the sum of fedTax, FICA, stateTax, SDI, fundAdmin, savings, dues and other (excluding travelSubs and fringes). grossThisProject, grossAllWork and netWagePaidWeek are stored as entered.

parameters.totalHrlyPayRate_X: hrlyPayRate_X + healthWelfare + vacationHoliday + pension + training + other
parameters.totalDeductions: fedTax + FICA + stateTax + SDI + fundAdmin + savings + dues + other

rules.verbatim_quote: totalDeductions is a source-of-truth field - it is stored directly and is not recalculated by the system. It must equal the sum of all deduction fields above and must not include travelSubs or fringe amounts.
rules.notes: Validation checks a tool should run before upload.

rules.title: eCPR XML V2: employee and classification fields
rules.plain_english: Each employee needs first and last name, street/city/2-letter state/ZIP, and a unique 9-digit SSN or ITIN. Each classification needs the official classification and craft names, employeeLevel ('journeyman' or 'apprentice'), apprenticeLevel 1-10 for apprentices, fringePaid flags (at least one true) and all five fringe amounts (0.0 if none).
rules.verbatim_quote: SSN takes priority when both ssn and itin are provided. At least one of ssn or itin must be populated. Each SSN must be unique within the submission - duplicate SSNs will cause the affected employees to be rejected.

rules.title: Certified payroll record contents and declaration
rules.plain_english: Each contractor and subcontractor must keep accurate payroll records showing each worker's name, address, Social Security number, work classification, straight-time and overtime hours each day and week, and actual per diem wages paid, verified under penalty of perjury that it is true and that LC 1771, 1811 and 1815 were complied with.

fields: straight time hours each day and week
overtime hours each day and week
parameters.form: DIR A-1-131 or equivalent printout with same info

rules.applies_to: All public works contractors and subcontractors
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) Each contractor and subcontractor shall keep accurate payroll records, showing the name, address, social security number, work classification, straight time and overtime hours worked each day and week, and the actual per diem wages paid to each journeyman, apprentice, worker, or other employee employed by the contractor or subcontractor in connection with the public work.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Also attach Statement of Employer Payments (DLSE Form PW 26) for fringe credits.

rules.title: Required certification wording for payroll copies
rules.plain_english: Certified payroll copies must carry a signed certification under penalty of perjury that the records are the originals or true, full and correct copies depicting actual disbursements to each worker.

parameters.template: I, [name], the undersigned, am [position] with the authority to act for and on behalf of [business], certify under penalty of perjury that the records or copies thereof submitted and consisting of [description, no. of pages] are the originals or true, full and correct copies of the originals which depict the payroll record(s) of the actual disbursements by way of cash, check, or whatever form to the individual or individuals named. Date: Signature:

rules.verbatim_quote: certify under penalty of perjury that the records or copies thereof submitted and consisting of ________________ (description, no. of pages) are the originals or true, full and correct copies of the originals which depict the payroll record(s) of the actual disbursements by way of cash, check, or whatever form to the individual or individuals named.
rules.notes: A public entity may require stricter certification. Electronic CPRs must be non-modifiable with e-signature or printed with original signature (8 CCR 16404(c)).

rules.title: CPRs must use the Director's classification title and full SSNs
rules.plain_english: Payroll records must name the worker's classification exactly as titled in DIR's prevailing wage determination (e.g., 'Laborer Group 1'), not just 'journeyman' or 'apprentice', and must include the full Social Security number (a separate sworn SSN report is accepted).
rules.source_location: https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/PWManualCombined.pdf (Public Works Manual Oct 2023, §3.1 and §3.1.13, manual pp. 13, 21)
rules.verbatim_quote: Payroll records which do not identify the Director’s specified title (e.g., records which only identify a worker by status, such as “journeyperson” or “apprentice” or “partner,” and do not refer to the Director’s published classification, such as “Laborer Group 1” or “Carpenter”) are inadequate.
rules.notes: Unlike LC 226 wage statements (last 4 SSN digits), LC 1776 requires the full SSN.

rules.title: Produce certified payroll within 10 days of a written request
rules.plain_english: When the awarding body, DLSE or DAS asks in writing, you must file certified copies of your payroll records within 10 days (calendar) of receiving the request. Workers can also request their own records.

requesters: public via awarding body or DLSE

rules.applies_to: All public works contractors and subcontractors
rules.verbatim_quote: (d) A contractor or subcontractor shall file a certified copy of the records enumerated in subdivision (a) with the entity that requested the records within 10 days after receipt of a written request.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Late payroll records: $100 per worker per calendar day
rules.plain_english: If you miss the 10-day deadline for requested payroll records, you forfeit $100 for each calendar day (or part) for each worker until you fully comply; DLSE can have it withheld from progress payments. A prime is not penalized for its sub's failure.
rules.applies_to: All public works contractors and subcontractors
rules.verbatim_quote: In the event that the contractor or subcontractor fails to comply within the 10-day period, the contractor or subcontractor shall, as a penalty to the state or political subdivision on whose behalf the contract is made or awarded, forfeit one hundred dollars ($100) for each calendar day, or portion thereof, for each worker, until strict compliance is effectuated.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. 8 CCR 16400(d)(2)(B) still recites an older $25/day figure; statute ($100) controls. SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1741, 1775, 1776, 1777.7 and 1813 to raise penalties/fees; final amounts and operative date NOT verified (bill analyses only) - re-check before 2027.

rules.title: Tell the awarding body where payroll records are kept (5 working days for changes)
rules.plain_english: The contractor must tell the awarding body the street address, city and county where its payroll records are kept and give notice of any change of location within five working days.
rules.verbatim_quote: (g) The contractor shall inform the body awarding the contract of the location of the records enumerated under subdivision (a), including the street address, city, and county, and shall, within five working days, provide a notice of a change of location and address.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Public requests for payroll: redaction and copying fees
rules.plain_english: Public requests for certified payroll go through the awarding body or DLSE, never directly to the contractor's office. Copies given to the public must black out workers' names, addresses and SSNs (not the contractor's name). The requester prepays $1 for the first page, $0.25 per additional page, plus $10 handling to the contractor.

parameters.taft_hartley_trust: redact only to last 4 SSN digits

rules.verbatim_quote: Such cost shall be $1 for the first page of the payroll record and 25 cents for each page thereafter, plus $10 to the contractor or subcontractor for handling costs. Payment in the form of cash, check or certified money order shall be made prior to release of the documents to cover the actual costs of preparation.
rules.notes: Public entity keeps received records at least 6 months after project completion and acceptance (16403(a)).

rules.title: Payroll record retention
rules.plain_english: Unregistered small-project contractors must keep certified payroll records at least 3 years after completing the work. For other projects the prevailing wage law sets no specific period; DLSE advises keeping them for the full limitations period (e.g., 18 months after notice of completion for assessments) and complying with general Labor Code/IWC record rules.
rules.source_location: https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/PWManualCombined.pdf (Public Works Manual Oct 2023, §3.1.14, manual p. 22); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf PDF page 961
rules.verbatim_quote: There is no provision in the prevailing wage laws which specifies a records retention period for CPRs or all of the types of “payroll records” as defined and listed at 8 CCR § 16000. The limitations period for legally recognized wage underpayment remedies available against public works contractors, however, vary depending upon the remedy available.
rules.notes: CSLB B&P 7111 separately requires keeping project records 5 years after completion (see lawbook research). General Labor Code payroll records: 3 years (see labor-hr research).

rules.title: Failing to produce payroll within 30 days of debarment notice: 1-3 year debarment
rules.plain_english: If you don't respond to a payroll request, the Labor Commissioner will notify you that you face debarment unless the records are produced within 30 days of receiving that notice; failing that (absent circumstances beyond your control), you are barred from public works for 1 to 3 years.
rules.verbatim_quote: the Labor Commissioner shall notify the contractor or subcontractor that, in addition to any other penalties provided by law, the contractor or subcontractor will be subject to debarment under this section if the certified payroll records are not produced within 30 days after receipt of the written notice.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Statement of Employer Payments (Form PW 26) for fringe credits
rules.plain_english: If you take credit for fringe benefit payments against the prevailing wage, document them on DLSE Form PW 26 (Statement of Employer Payments) along with the A-1-131 payroll form; accurate completion of both is presumptive compliance on CMU-monitored projects.

parameters.companion_form: DIR Form A-1-131 Public Works Payroll Reporting Form

rules.verbatim_quote: Payroll records shall be furnished in a format prescribed by section 16401 of Title 8 of the California Code of Regulations, with use of the current version of DIR’s “Public Works Payroll Reporting Form” (A-1-131) and “Statement of Employer Payments” (DLSE Form PW26) constituting presumptive compliance with this requirement
rules.notes: 16461 applies to CMU-fee projects; DLSE also encloses A-1-131 and PW 26 with every written CPR request (Manual §3.1.5).

rules.title: Ready-mix concrete haulers: written subcontract requiring prevailing wage compliance
rules.plain_english: A company hauling/delivering ready-mixed concrete to a public works project must have a written subcontract agreement with whoever engaged it that requires compliance with the prevailing wage chapter; it is a subcontractor only for prevailing wage purposes (must register, pay prevailing wages, file eCPRs).

parameters.must_require: compliance with Labor Code Part 7, Chapter 1 (public works)
parameters.status: subcontractor solely for prevailing wage chapter

rules.applies_to: Ready-mix suppliers and the contractors who order from them
rules.verbatim_quote: (e) The entity hauling or delivering ready-mixed concrete to carry out a public works contract shall enter into a written subcontract agreement with the party that engaged the entity to supply the ready-mixed concrete. The written agreement shall require compliance with the requirements of this chapter.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. DIR FAQ: an invoice or purchase order with the required statutory language may suffice.

rules.title: Ready-mix: certified payroll to engaging party and GC within 5 working days
rules.plain_english: The ready-mix hauler must give certified payroll copies to the party that engaged it and to the general contractor within five working days after the employee is paid, with a time record certified by each driver.
rules.applies_to: Ready-mix concrete suppliers on public works
rules.verbatim_quote: (f) The entity hauling or delivering ready-mixed concrete to carry out a public works contract shall submit a certified copy of the payroll records required by subdivision (a) of Section 1776 to the party that engaged the entity and to the general contractor within five working days after the employee has been paid, accompanied by a written time record that shall be certified by each driver
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. DIR FAQ: no statutory penalty for missing the 5 days; contract may impose one.

rules.title: Ready-mix: rate from the plant's area; covers loading through return trip
rules.plain_english: Ready-mix drivers are paid the 'Driver - Mixer Trucks' prevailing rate for the area where the plant is located, from receiving concrete at the plant until returning to the plant (intermediate private stops included).

parameters.covered_time: receipt of concrete at plant through return to plant

rules.verbatim_quote: (d) For purposes of this section, the applicable prevailing wage rate shall be the current prevailing wage, as determined by the director, for the geographic area in which the factory or batching plant is located.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Prevailing wage determinations: issued Feb 22 / Aug 22, effective 10 days later
rules.plain_english: DIR issues general prevailing wage determinations twice a year, on February 22 and August 22. Each takes effect 10 days after its issue date (generally March 4 (March 3 in leap years) and September 1).
rules.verbatim_quote: General determinations are issued twice a year on February 22 and August 22.
rules.notes: FAQ A10: effective date 'is 10 days after the issue date of the determination.' Rates: https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/DPreWageDetermination.htm

rules.title: Which rates apply: those in effect on the bid advertisement date
rules.plain_english: Use the determination in effect on the date the awarding body first advertised for bids (or, if not bid, the first written agreement/funding contract). A later change in the Director's rates does not apply to a contract whose notice to bidders was already published (but see predetermined increases and the 2027 large-project rule).

parameters.rate_lock_event: bid advertisement date (first published notice inviting bids)
parameters.fallback_event_if_not_bid: first written memorialization of agreement or funding contract

rules.applies_to: Estimators and payroll on public works
rules.citation: Labor Code 1773.6; 8 CCR 16000 ('Date of Notice or Call for Bids')
rules.verbatim_quote: For the Labor Commissioner’s enforcement purposes, if the effective date of a determination is on or after the bid advertisement date but before the listed expiration date, the rates listed on that particular determination constitute the prevailing wage rates for work performed under that public works contract.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. LC 1773.6: a Director's change 'shall not be effective as to any contract for which the notice to bidders has been published.' See rule ab1198-mid-project-rate-changes-35m (not verified).

rules.title: Double-asterisk determinations: pay scheduled increases mid-project
rules.plain_english: If a determination's expiration date has two asterisks (**), predetermined increases to base rates, overtime, holiday pay and employer payments must be paid for work after that date - build them into bids. A single asterisk (*) means the rates stay in effect for the life of the project.

parameters.double_asterisk: predetermined increases must be paid after expiration date; new rate effective day after expiration date
parameters.single_asterisk: rates in effect at bid advertisement apply for life of project

rules.citation: 8 CCR 16000 ('Predetermined Changes'); DIR Prevailing Wage FAQ
rules.verbatim_quote: Prevailing wage determinations with double asterisks after the expiration date indicate that the basic hourly wage rate, overtime, holiday pay rates and employers' payments for work performed after this date have been predetermined. If work is to extend past this date, the new rates must be paid and should be incorporated in contracts entered into now.
rules.notes: Predetermined increases are posted on DIR's OD-Research pages.

rules.title: Special wage determination request: 45 days before bid advertisement
rules.plain_english: If a needed craft or classification is not covered by a general determination, the awarding body should request a special determination at least 45 days before the bid advertisement date.
rules.applies_to: Awarding bodies; contractors spotting missing classifications
rules.verbatim_quote: (B) If a wage rate for a craft, classification or type of worker is not published in the Director's general prevailing wage determinations, a request for a special determination should be made by the awarding body to Chief, Division of Labor Statistics and Research, P.O. Box 420603, San Francisco, CA 94142, at least 45 days prior to the project bid advertisement date.

rules.title: Petition to review a wage rate within 20 days after bid advertising starts
rules.plain_english: A prospective bidder, union representative or the awarding body may file a verified petition with the DIR Director within 20 days after bid advertising begins, copying the awarding body within 2 days. The Director decides within 20 days, and the bid closing is extended until 5 days after the determination.
rules.verbatim_quote: Any prospective bidder or his representative, any representative of any craft, classification or type of workman involved, or the awarding body may, within 20 days after commencement of advertising of the call for bids by the awarding body, file with the Director of Industrial Relations a verified petition to review the determination of any such rate or rates
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. AB 1198 (2026) reportedly creates a new 20-day petition process - not verified.

rules.title: Large projects ($35M+): mid-project prevailing wage changes from July 1, 2027 (reported)
rules.plain_english: Reported new law: starting July 1, 2027, changes in prevailing wage rates apply mid-project to public works prime contracts awarded at $35 million or more, instead of staying fixed at bid-time rates. Who bears the cost is not addressed.
rules.applies_to: Contractors bidding very large public works
rules.citation: Labor Code 1773.6 et seq. as amended by AB 1198 (2026) - unverified
rules.notes: From web-search summary of a law-firm alert and bill trackers; chaptered text not read (leginfo unreachable). Do not rely on threshold or date until verified against Ch. 513, Stats. 2026.

rules.title: Public works overtime: over 8 hours/day or 40 hours/week at 1.5x
rules.plain_english: Work on public works over 8 hours in a day or 40 hours in a week must be paid at least 1.5 times the basic rate, or the higher overtime rate in the wage determination (some crafts trigger overtime sooner, e.g., 7/35).
rules.verbatim_quote: Labor Code § 1815 requires that work performed on public works projects in excess of 8 hours per day, or 40 hours per week, must be compensated at not less than time and one-half the basic rate of pay. Failure to pay the appropriate overtime rates subject the contractor to penalties pursuant to Labor Code § 1813.
rules.notes: LC 1815 text itself not read (leginfo unreachable); statement taken from official DLSE Public Works Manual and 8 CCR 16100(b)(8).

rules.title: Limited exceptions to weekend overtime
rules.plain_english: No overtime is owed for the first 8 hours on Saturday or Sunday only if (1) a non-Monday-Friday workweek is a fixed business practice on all your jobs or required by the awarding body, (2) the CBA allows straight-time weekend work, or (3) the awarding body finds off-hours work necessary; otherwise follow the determination.

exceptions: fixed business practice/awarding body requires non Mon-Fri workweek: first 8 hrs Sat/Sun straight time
CBA provides Sat/Sun straight time: first 8 hrs
awarding body determines off-hours work necessary: no OT first 8 hrs/day and 40 hrs/week
no OT under 8/day or 40/week unless CBA basis requires

rules.applies_to: Public works employers scheduling weekend work
rules.verbatim_quote: If a workweek other than Monday through Friday is a fixed business practice or is required by the awarding body, no overtime payment is required for the first eight hours on Saturday or Sunday.
rules.notes: Saturday make-up day exceptions apply only if written into the determination itself (Manual §4.1.9).

rules.title: Alternative workweek schedules don't avoid daily overtime on public works
rules.plain_english: Even workers on a 4/10 alternative workweek or under a CBA must get overtime for hours over 8 in a day on public works.
rules.applies_to: Contractors using 4/10 or other AWS schedules
rules.citation: Labor Code 1810, 1811, 1815; Cal. Const. art. XIV §2
rules.verbatim_quote: Accordingly, no worker may be employed on a public works project for more than eight hours a day unless the worker receives the overtime compensation specified by the applicable prevailing wage determination.

rules.title: Overtime when a worker works two classifications or projects in a day
rules.plain_english: All hours in a day count toward overtime; overtime hours are paid at the overtime rate for the classification being worked during those hours. For mixed public/private days, public-work overtime uses the higher of the prevailing rate or weighted average.

parameters.ot_rate: classification worked during the OT hours
parameters.public_private_mix: higher of weighted-average regular rate or prevailing rate
parameters.example: 4h Inside Wireman ST + 4h Painter ST + 2h Painter OT

rules.applies_to: Payroll for multi-craft or mixed public/private crews
rules.citation: Labor Code 1815; DLSE Public Works Manual
rules.verbatim_quote: In the situation where a worker performs work during the same workday in two or more different classifications with different rates of pay, the worker must be paid the overtime rate in effect for the type of work he or she is performing during those overtime hours.

rules.title: Travel time is paid at the prevailing rate; travel/subsistence payments per determination
rules.plain_english: Employer-required travel after the first reporting place (yard to site, site to site) is hours worked paid at the prevailing rate for the work performed. Separately, many determinations require fixed daily travel and/or subsistence payments - check the footnotes.

parameters.travel_time_rate: prevailing rate for work performed at site unless determination sets lower travel rate
parameters.travel_subsistence_payments: fixed daily amounts per CBA footnotes on determination

rules.citation: Labor Code 1773.1(a)(4)-(5); DLSE Public Works Manual
rules.verbatim_quote: All such compensable travel time must be paid at the same prevailing wage rate required for the work actually performed by the worker at the public works site.
rules.notes: Report travel/subsistence on eCPR as travelSubs (not a deduction).

rules.title: Fringe credits cannot reduce the basic hourly rate
rules.plain_english: Employer payments (health, pension, vacation, training, etc.) count toward the total prevailing wage package, but they can never reduce the straight-time or overtime basic hourly rate shown in the determination; no credit for benefits required by other law.

no_credit_for: benefits required by other state/federal law
industry advancement fees not under obligated CBA

rules.verbatim_quote: (c) Employer payments are a credit against the obligation to pay the general prevailing rate of per diem wages. However, credit shall not be granted for benefits required to be provided by other state or federal law,
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Same subdivision: 'Credits for employer payments also shall not reduce the obligation to pay the hourly straight time or overtime wages found to be prevailing.'

rules.title: Fringe credit allowed if contributions are made at least quarterly
rules.plain_english: You may take credit for employer payments even if they are not paid in the same pay period, as long as you regularly make the contributions at least quarterly.
rules.verbatim_quote: (d) An employer may take credit for an employer payment specified in subdivision (b), even if contributions are not made, or costs are not paid, during the same pay period for which credit is taken, if the employer regularly makes the contributions, or regularly pays the costs, for the plan, fund, or program on no less than a quarterly basis.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Annualize fringe credits when public-job contributions exceed private-job ones
rules.plain_english: If you pay higher benefit contributions on public jobs than on private jobs, the credit must be annualized: divide annual plan cost by total hours worked on all jobs (DLSE accepts 2,080 hours unless the worker worked more). Exceptions: enforceable obligation for future private work, PLA requirement, CAC payments, or Director waiver.

exceptions: enforceable obligation to pay higher rate on future private work

rules.verbatim_quote: (e) The credit for employer payments shall be computed on an annualized basis when the employer seeks credit for employer payments that are higher for public works projects than for private construction performed by the same employer,
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Manual: 'It is not considered a violation if the contractor uses the full year equivalent of 2,080 (40 hours x 52 weeks) hours ... unless ... the affected employee worked more than 2,080 hours'.

rules.title: Underpaying prevailing wages: up to $200 per worker per day
rules.plain_english: For each worker paid less than the prevailing rate, the contractor and sub forfeit up to $200 per calendar day (or part). Minimums: $40 (unless a good-faith mistake promptly corrected), $80 if penalized in the prior 3 years, $120 if willful. Back wages are also owed and wages are satisfied before penalties.

parameters.plus: difference between prevailing and paid wages to each worker

rules.verbatim_quote: forfeit not more than two hundred dollars ($200) for each calendar day, or portion thereof, for each worker paid less than the prevailing wage rates as determined by the director for the work or craft in which the worker is employed for any public work done under the contract by the contractor or, except as provided in subdivision (b), by any subcontractor under the contractor.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1741, 1775, 1776, 1777.7 and 1813 to raise penalties/fees; final amounts and operative date NOT verified (bill analyses only) - re-check before 2027. (SB 909 analyses mention raising $200/$120 maximum/minimums - e.g., to $280/$168 - unverified.)

rules.title: Overtime violations: $25 per worker per day (mandatory)
rules.plain_english: For each worker each calendar day the worker is required or permitted to work over 8 hours in a day or 40 in a week without proper overtime, the contractor forfeits $25. The Labor Commissioner cannot waive or reduce it.

parameters.trigger: work over 8 hrs/day or 40 hrs/week without required OT pay

rules.verbatim_quote: The dollar amount of this penalty is fixed at $25.00 for each worker for each calendar day during which the worker is required or permitted to work more than eight hours in any one calendar day or 40 hours in any one calendar week.
rules.notes: LC 1813 text not read; amount from DLSE Public Works Manual (Oct 2023). SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1741, 1775, 1776, 1777.7 and 1813 to raise penalties/fees; final amounts and operative date NOT verified (bill analyses only) - re-check before 2027. (SB 909 analysis described $25 -> $35 - unverified.)

rules.title: Subcontracts must include LC 1771, 1775, 1776, 1777.5, 1813 and 1815
rules.plain_english: To avoid penalties for a sub's underpayment, the prime's written subcontract must include a copy of Labor Code sections 1771, 1775, 1776, 1777.5, 1813 and 1815.

parameters.where: contract between prime and each subcontractor

rules.verbatim_quote: (1) The contract executed between the contractor and the subcontractor for the performance of work on the public works project shall include a copy of the provisions of this section and Sections 1771, 1776, 1777.5, 1813, and 1815.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Safe harbor does not apply if prime knew of the underpayment; prime remains jointly liable for wages, 1813 penalties and liquidated damages.

rules.title: Prime must monitor sub payroll, act on violations, and get a sworn affidavit before final payment
rules.plain_english: The prime must periodically review each sub's certified payroll, take corrective action (including withholding funds) on discovering underpayment, and before final payment obtain the sub's affidavit under penalty of perjury that it paid prevailing wages and any 1813 amounts.

steps: periodic review of sub certified payrolls
diligent corrective action incl. retaining sufficient funds
affidavit under penalty of perjury before final payment
