affidavit_contents: sub paid general prevailing rate of per diem wages to employees on the project
sub paid any amounts due under LC 1813
parameters.timing: prior to final payment to subcontractor

rules.verbatim_quote: (4) Prior to making final payment to the subcontractor for work performed on the public works project, the contractor shall obtain an affidavit signed under penalty of perjury from the subcontractor that the subcontractor has paid the specified general prevailing rate of per diem wages to his or her employees on the public works project and any amounts due pursuant to Section 1813.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. A tool can generate this affidavit and block final sub payment until it is on file.

rules.title: DLSE notifies the prime within 15 days of a complaint about a sub
rules.plain_english: When DLSE receives a complaint that a subcontractor is underpaying prevailing wages, it must notify the prime contractor within 15 days - a trigger for the prime's corrective-action duty.

parameters.trigger: DLSE receipt of complaint about subcontractor underpayment

rules.verbatim_quote: (c) The Division of Labor Standards Enforcement shall notify the contractor on a public works project within 15 days of the receipt by the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement of a complaint of the failure of a subcontractor on that public works project to pay workers the general prevailing rate of per diem wages.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Prime and subs are jointly and severally liable for unpaid prevailing wages
rules.plain_english: Contractors and subcontractors share responsibility for all money due from a violation; even a prime that meets the 1775(b) safe harbor remains liable for its subs' unpaid wages, 1813 penalties and liquidated damages.
rules.verbatim_quote: Contractors and subcontractors share monetary responsibility (known as joint and several liability) for all monies due as a result of a violation.
rules.notes: LC 1784 lets a private-job contractor recover costs from its hiring party in limited cases.

rules.title: No wage kickbacks or fees for hiring/registration on public works
rules.plain_english: Contractors may not take back any part of workers' wages (kickbacks) or charge fees for registering anyone for public work or filling work orders.

prohibited: taking/receiving any portion of workers' wages (LC 1778)
fees for registering persons for public work (LC 1779)

rules.verbatim_quote: (6) The prohibition against accepting or extracting kickback from employee wages under Labor Code Section 1778; (7) The prohibition against accepting fees for registering any person for public work under Labor Code Section 1779; or for filling work orders on public works under Labor Code Section 1780;
rules.notes: Statute text not read; prohibition confirmed by DIR regulation checklist. DIR lists 'Demands that worker pay wage kickbacks' as a common violation.

rules.title: Workers' compensation: required clause and signed certification before starting work
rules.plain_english: Every public works contract must require the contractor to secure workers' compensation for employees (LC 3700), and the contractor must sign and file a certification with the awarding body before starting work.

parameters.certification_text_reported: I am aware of the provisions of Section 3700 of the Labor Code which require every employer to be insured against liability for workers' compensation or to undertake self-insurance in accordance with the provisions of that code, and I will comply with such provisions before commencing the performance of the work of this contract.

rules.source_location: Secondary (search snippets of LC 1861); DIR regulation https://www.dir.ca.gov/t8/16100.html (c)(3) and https://www.dir.ca.gov/t8/16421_appendixA.html item (11)
rules.notes: Requirement confirmed in DIR regs (16100(c)(3): 'Provide workers' compensation coverage as set forth in Labor Code Section 1861'); certification wording comes from search-engine excerpts, not the official statute text - verify before generating the form.

rules.title: Prejob conference labor-law checklist and subcontractor acknowledgment
rules.plain_english: Awarding bodies (especially with labor compliance programs) review a standard list of labor requirements at the prejob conference and may have each subcontractor sign an acknowledgment that it was informed of them.

parameters.acknowledgment: I acknowledge that I have been informed and am aware of the foregoing requirements and that I am authorized to make this certification on behalf of [name of subcontractor].

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors at prejob meetings
rules.verbatim_quote: I acknowledge that I have been informed and am aware of the foregoing requirements and that I am authorized to make this certification on behalf of [name of subcontractor].
rules.notes: Labeled 'Suggested Checklist'; useful template for document generation.

rules.title: Apprenticeship duties apply on public works of $30,000 or more
rules.plain_english: On public works contracts of $30,000 or more, every contractor and subcontractor employing workers in an apprenticeable craft must meet the apprenticeship requirements, even if its own subcontract is under $30,000. General contractors (and specialty primes) with contracts under $30,000 are exempt.

exempt_when: federal project with no state/local funds not administered by state agency
sole proprietor who worked alone with no employees

rules.verbatim_quote: (o) This section does not apply to contracts of general contractors or to contracts of specialty contractors not bidding for work through a general or prime contractor when the contracts of general contractors or those specialty contractors involve less than thirty thousand dollars ($30,000).
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. DAS FAQ: training fund contributions are still owed on projects under $30,000 (paid to employee only if exempt).

rules.title: DAS 140 contract award information: within 10 days of contract execution
rules.plain_english: Send contract award information (DAS 140 or equivalent written notice) to the applicable apprenticeship committee(s) within 10 days after your prime contract or subcontract is executed, and no later than the first day you have workers on the job. Failure is a continuing violation until the notice of completion.

parameters.latest: first day contractor has workers employed on the public work
parameters.dlse_enforcement_deadline: first day a journeyperson in that craft works for the contractor
parameters.continuing_violation_until: awarding body files Notice of Completion

rules.verbatim_quote: The information shall be provided to the applicable apprenticeship committee within ten (10) days of the date of the execution of the prime contract or subcontract, but in no event later than the first day in which the contractor has workers employed upon the public work.
rules.notes: DAS FAQ: sending DAS 140/142 after the project ends does not eliminate penalties. Exempt contractors under 1777.5(j)/(k) certificates still must send DAS 140.

rules.title: Who gets the DAS 140
rules.plain_english: If you are already approved to train apprentices, send it to your apprenticeship committee for the craft; if not, send it to every apprenticeship committee whose area covers the job site, for each craft you will use. Do not send it to DAS.

parameters.approved_to_train: your committee(s) for each craft in area
parameters.not_approved: ALL applicable committees in geographic area for each craft

form_boxes.2: comply with a committee's standards for this job only
form_boxes.3: follow California Apprenticeship Council regulations (1:5 min and max)

rules.applies_to: All contractors/subcontractors on covered public works
rules.verbatim_quote: Contractors who are not already approved to train by an apprenticeship program sponsor shall provide contract award information to all of the applicable apprenticeship committees whose geographic area of operation includes the area of the public works project.

rules.title: DAS 140 required contents
rules.plain_english: The contract award notice must state: contractor name, address, phone and license number; awarding body name and address; exact job location; contract award date; expected start date; estimated journeyman hours; number of apprentices to be employed; and approximate dates they will be employed.

fields: awarding body full name and address
exact location of public work site
number of apprentices to be employed
approximate dates apprentices will be employed

rules.verbatim_quote: (1) the contractor's name, address, telephone number and state license number; (2) full name and address of the public work awarding body; (3) the exact location of the public work site; (4) date of the contract award; (5) expected start date of the work; (6) estimated journeyman hours; (7) number of apprentices to be employed; (8) approximate dates apprentices will be employed;
rules.notes: DAS 140 is not a dispatch request; a separate DAS 142 is required.

rules.title: DAS 142 apprentice dispatch request: written, at least 72 hours ahead
rules.plain_english: If you don't already employ enough registered apprentices, request dispatch in writing (first-class mail, fax or email) from the apprenticeship committees for the craft at least 72 hours (excluding Saturdays, Sundays and holidays) before you need them. If one committee doesn't dispatch, request from each other committee in the area.

parameters.escalation: request from every committee in area (consecutively or simultaneously) until all asked
parameters.frequency: once per project per craft (DAS FAQ)

rules.verbatim_quote: must request the dispatch of required apprentices from the apprenticeship committees providing training in the applicable craft or trade and whose geographic area of operation includes the site of the public work by giving the committee written notice of at least 72 hours (excluding Saturdays, Sundays and holidays) before the date on which one or more apprentices are required.
rules.notes: Requests must be unconditional (no circumventing duty to pay for preemployment processes). Contractor need not sign DAS 7 or other conditions (DAS FAQ).

rules.title: Dispatch requests: at least an 8-hour day or 20% of apprentice hours
rules.plain_english: Except on jobs with under 40 journeyman hours, each dispatch request must be for at least an 8-hour day per apprentice or 20% of the estimated apprentice hours for that craft, whichever is greater.
rules.verbatim_quote: Except for projects with less than 40 hours of journeyman work, each request for apprentice dispatch shall be for not less than an 8 hour day per each apprentice, or 20% of the estimated apprentice hours to be worked for an employer in a particular craft or trade on a project, whichever is greater,

rules.title: DAS 142 required contents
rules.plain_english: A dispatch request must include: request date; committee name, address, phone and fax/email; contractor name, address, CSLB license number, phone and fax/email; project name and address; DIR project number, contract number, total contract and subcontract amounts; number of apprentices, craft, report date (72-hour notice), report time, person and address to report to.

fields: name of person to report to
parameters.form: DAS 142 (Rev. 6/24) optional; one craft per form

rules.verbatim_quote: 5) PWC Project Number, Contract Number, Total Contract Amount, Sub-Contract Amount for projects which have been registered with the Department of Industrial Relations in accordance with Labor Code section 1773.3; 6) Dispatch Request Information: Number of Apprentice(s) Needed, Craft or Trade, Date Apprentice(s) to Report (72 hrs. notice required), Time to Report, Name of Person to Report to

rules.title: Minimum ratio: 1 apprentice hour per 5 journeyman hours, per craft, by end of contract
rules.plain_english: By the end of your contract or subcontract, apprentice hours in each apprenticeable craft must be at least 20% of the straight-time journeyman hours in that craft (1:5). Hours over 8/day or 40/week don't count, crafts can't be combined, and you should try to employ apprentices while journeymen are on site.

parameters.max_ratio: per committee standards if contractor bound by them; CAC rules: max = min = 1:5

rules.applies_to: All contractors/subcontractors employing apprenticeable crafts on covered public works
rules.verbatim_quote: However, except as otherwise provided in this section, in no case shall the ratio be less than one hour of apprentice work for every five hours of journeyman work.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. DAS FAQ example: 100 journeyman hours -> 20 apprentice hours. Manual example: 750 ST journeyman hrs -> 150 apprentice hrs.

rules.title: Ratio shortfall defense: proper DAS 142 requests
rules.plain_english: If you fall short of the 1:5 ratio, you avoid penalties only by proving you made timely written dispatch requests (72-hour notice) to every committee in the area, early enough to meet the ratio, kept proof of sending, and employed every apprentice dispatched.

must_prove: requested from each committee in area
copy of each written request with proof sent by mail/fax/email
at least 72 hours notice excl. weekends/holidays
requested in time to meet ratio

rules.verbatim_quote: To do so, it is the contractor's burden to establish that all of the regulation's request-to-dispatch requirements have been satisfied.
rules.notes: Retain DAS 142 transmittal proofs (fax confirmations, email receipts, certified mail receipts).

rules.title: Only DAS-registered apprentices may be paid apprentice rates
rules.plain_english: Only workers registered in a DAS-approved apprenticeship program, with a written apprentice agreement, may be paid apprentice rates. Anyone else doing the craft's work must be paid the journeyman rate, and does not count toward the ratio.

parameters.eligible: apprentices under DAS-approved standards with written agreement (LC 3077)

rules.verbatim_quote: (c) Only apprentices, as defined in Section 3077, who are in training under apprenticeship standards that have been approved by the Chief of the Division of Apprenticeship Standards and who are parties to written apprentice agreements under Chapter 4 (commencing with Section 3070) of Division 3 are eligible to be employed at the apprentice wage rate on public works.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Helpers may never replace statutorily required apprentices (8 CCR 16000).

rules.title: Apprentices: apprentice prevailing rate, own craft only, journeyperson supervision
rules.plain_english: Apprentices must be paid the apprentice prevailing rate for their trade, may only do work of the craft they are registered in, and (under CAC rules / DAS 140 box 3) must always work with or under direct supervision of a journeyperson - otherwise the journeyman rate is owed.

parameters.pay: apprentice prevailing per diem rate for registered trade
parameters.work_scope: only craft/work processes in apprenticeship standards
parameters.supervision: at all times with or under direct supervision of journeyworker (CAC rules)

rules.verbatim_quote: Where an employer employs apprentices under the rules and regulations of the California Apprenticeship Council, as set forth in Labor Code Section 1777.5(c)(2), apprentices employed on public works must at all times work with or under the direct supervision of a journeyworker.
rules.notes: Apprentice rates: https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/pwappwage/PWAppWageStart.asp

rules.title: Pay apprentices for required pre-employment testing/training time
rules.plain_english: If you require a dispatched apprentice to fill out an application, test, train or undergo other pre-employment processes, you must pay the apprentice prevailing rate for that time and related travel (not if they fail a required drug/alcohol test), unless a CBA provides otherwise.

parameters.exception: failed pre-employment drug or alcohol test

rules.verbatim_quote: the apprentice shall be paid for the time spent on the required preemployment activity, including travel time to and from the required activity, if any, at the prevailing rate of per diem wages for apprentices in the trade to which he or she is registered.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Training fund contributions: every hour, due the 15th of the next month
rules.plain_english: For every hour worked by journeymen and apprentices in an apprenticeable craft (including overtime), pay the training contribution shown on the wage determination to the CAC (with Form CAC-2) or an approved apprenticeship program. Payments are due by the 15th of the month after the work, and cannot be paid to the worker instead.

parameters.rate_source: training amount on prevailing wage determination
parameters.hours_covered: all hours incl. overtime, journeymen and apprentices, apprenticeable crafts
payee_options: approved apprenticeship program serving the site (credit)
parameters.cac_mail: DIR - California Apprenticeship Council, P.O. Box 511283, Los Angeles, CA 90051-7838

rules.applies_to: All contractors employing apprenticeable crafts on public works
rules.verbatim_quote: (b) Training contributions to the Council are due and payable on the 15th day of each month for work performed during the preceding month.
rules.notes: DAS FAQ: paying the training amount to employees does not satisfy the obligation and is not recoverable; on exempt (<$30,000) projects training fund is paid to employee.

rules.title: CAC-2 training fund remittance contents
rules.plain_english: Training contribution checks to the CAC must be accompanied by Form CAC-2 or equivalent information: contractor name/address/phone and license number, awarding agency, jobsite and county, contract/project number, period covered, contribution rate and hours by occupation, programs that provided apprentices, and apprentice hours by occupation and program.

rules.plain_english: Within 60 days after concluding work on the contract, each contractor and subcontractor must give the apprenticeship program (and the awarding body if requested) a verified statement of journeyman and apprentice hours performed.
rules.verbatim_quote: Within 60 days after concluding work on the contract, each contractor and subcontractor shall submit to the awarding body, if requested, and to the apprenticeship program a verified statement of the journeyman and apprentice hours performed on the contract.

rules.title: Apprenticeship violations: up to $100/day ($300/day for repeats) plus possible debarment
rules.plain_english: Knowing violations of apprenticeship requirements (DAS 140, ratio, training funds) carry civil penalties up to $100 per full calendar day of noncompliance, rising to up to $300 per day for two or more violations within 3 years, plus possible debarment.
rules.verbatim_quote: § 1777.7(a)(1) provides that contractors who knowingly violate any of the apprenticeship standards found in § 1777.5 “shall forfeit as a civil penalty” an amount not exceeding $100 “for each full calendar day of noncompliance.” (Note that the maximum increases to $300 per day when two or more violations occur within a three-year period.

rules.title: Counting DAS 140 penalty days
rules.plain_english: The first penalty day is the day after the deadline (first day a journeyperson in that craft worked). Penalties run each calendar day until the DAS 140 is sent, or if never sent, through the last day the contractor did apprenticeable work on the project.

parameters.first_penalty_day: day after first day journeyperson in craft worked
parameters.last_penalty_day_if_never_sent: last day contractor performed apprenticeable work

rules.title: Ratio exemption certificates
rules.plain_english: DAS may exempt a contractor from the 1:5 ratio for a craft if it averages at least 1:5 on all its California contracts annually; an apprenticeship program may grant (subject to DAS approval) an exemption if area unemployment over 3 months exceeds 15%, apprentices in the area exceed 1:5, the craft replaces 1/30 of journeymen annually through apprenticeship, or safety prevents apprentice assignment.
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) Unemployment for the previous three-month period in the area exceeds an average of 15 percent. (2) The number of apprentices in training in the area exceeds a ratio of 1 to 5. (3) There is a showing that the apprenticeable craft or trade is replacing at least one-thirtieth of its journeymen annually through apprenticeship training,

rules.title: Contracts must make the prime responsible for apprenticeship compliance
rules.plain_english: The awarding body must insert contract stipulations implementing LC 1777.5 that fix responsibility for compliance for all apprenticeable occupations on the prime contractor; similarly 1775 and 1776 stipulations must be in the contract.
rules.applies_to: Awarding bodies; prime contractors flowing down
rules.verbatim_quote: (n) The body awarding the contract shall cause to be inserted in the contract stipulations to effectuate this section. The stipulations shall fix the responsibility of compliance with this section for all apprenticeable occupations with the prime contractor.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Debarment: fraud (1-3 years) or two willful violations in 3 years (up to 3 years)
rules.plain_english: A contractor found to violate prevailing wage law with intent to defraud is barred from bidding or subcontracting on public works for 1 to 3 years; two or more separate willful violations within 3 years can bring up to 3 years. 'Willful' means it knew or should have known its obligations and deliberately failed or refused to comply.

parameters.extends_to: entities in which contractor has any interest; responsible officers/managers

rules.verbatim_quote: (e) A willful violation occurs when the contractor or subcontractor knew or reasonably should have known of his or her obligations under the public works law and deliberately fails or deliberately refuses to comply with its provisions.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Debarred list: https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/debar.html (check before listing/hiring subs).

rules.title: Debarment for knowing serious apprenticeship violations (1 yr / 3 yrs)
rules.plain_english: Knowingly committing a serious violation of LC 1777.5 can bar the contractor and its responsible officers for up to 1 year for a first violation and up to 3 years for later violations.
rules.verbatim_quote: the Labor Commissioner may also deny to the contractor or subcontractor, and to its responsible officers, the right to bid on or to be awarded or perform work as a subcontractor on any public works contract for a period of up to one year for the first violation and for a period of up to three years for a second or subsequent violation.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Do not use debarred subcontractors
rules.plain_english: Public works contracts must prohibit the contractor from performing work with a subcontractor ineligible under LC 1777.1 or 1777.7; a subcontract with a debarred sub is reportedly void and public money paid to it must be returned. A listed sub who becomes ineligible may be substituted.

rules.title: Wage assessments must be served within 18 months after notice of completion or acceptance
rules.plain_english: The Labor Commissioner must serve a Civil Wage and Penalty Assessment within 18 months after a valid notice of completion is recorded or the work is accepted, whichever is later; the period is tolled while you fail to produce requested payroll.

parameters.trigger: later of recorded valid notice of completion or acceptance of the public work
tolled_during: awarding body failure to furnish NOC/acceptance

rules.applies_to: Contractors assessing exposure after project close-out
rules.verbatim_quote: Labor Code § 1741 provides that the CWPA shall be served not later than 18 months after the filing of a valid notice of completion in the office of the county recorder in which the public work was performed, or not later than 18 months after acceptance of the public work, whichever occurs last.

rules.title: Request review of a wage assessment within 60 days or it becomes final
rules.plain_english: If you don't file a written request for a review hearing within 60 days after service of a Civil Wage and Penalty Assessment, it becomes final and can be collected from withheld contract funds or entered as a court judgment.

parameters.if_missed: assessment final; collect from awarding body withholding or court judgment

rules.title: Settlement meeting: request within 30 days of a CWPA
rules.plain_english: Within 30 days after service of a CWPA (or an awarding body's notice of withholding), the contractor may request a settlement meeting, which must be held before the 60-day review deadline; statements made are confidential.
rules.applies_to: Contractors served with a CWPA or notice of withholding
rules.verbatim_quote: The Labor Commissioner shall, upon receipt of a request from the affected contractor or subcontractor within 30 days following the service of a civil wage and penalty assessment under Section 1741, afford the contractor or subcontractor the opportunity to meet with the Labor Commissioner or his or her designee to attempt to settle a dispute regarding the assessment

rules.title: Liquidated damages equal to unpaid wages after 60 days (avoid by escrow deposit)
rules.plain_english: Wages still unpaid 60 days after service of a CWPA or notice of withholding make the contractor, sub and surety liable for liquidated damages equal to those wages. You avoid this by depositing the full assessment (including penalties) with DIR in escrow within the 60 days.

parameters.avoid_by: deposit full assessment incl. penalties with DIR within 60 days

rules.title: Joint labor-management committee lawsuits within 18 months
rules.plain_english: A joint labor-management committee may sue an employer that fails to pay prevailing wages or provide payroll records, up to 18 months after the notice of completion or acceptance (whichever is later); courts award back wages, interest and equal liquidated damages.

parameters.trigger: later of recorded notice of completion or acceptance
remedies: liquidated damages equal to unpaid wages

rules.title: Prop 84-funded projects: CPRs to both DIR and the LCP
rules.plain_english: Projects funded by Proposition 84 still require a DIR-approved labor compliance program; contractors must submit certified payroll to both DIR (eCPR) and the LCP.

rules.verbatim_quote: Contractors on these Proposition 84 projects must submit certified payroll records to both the DIR and the LCP.

rules.title: Attorney General action against licenses for unpaid wages; good-faith wage-rate mistake not a violation
rules.plain_english: Effective 2026, the Attorney General may sue to have CSLB suspend, revoke or deny a license when a contractor fails to pay workers wages owed, a wage judgment, or a wage injunction. A good-faith mistake about which wage rate applies (including prevailing wage) is not a violation under this section.

grounds: failure to pay full wages owed

Final amounts and start date were not verified; until confirmed, current amounts in this file apply.

rules.title: Skilled & trained workforce (STW) applies only when a statute or the awarding body requires it
rules.plain_english: STW rules (PCC 2600-2603) apply when a specific statute/regulation requires an enforceable STW commitment or the awarding body chooses to require it. They are independent of prevailing wage coverage; bid documents should give notice, but missing notice does not excuse compliance.

triggers: statute or regulation requiring STW commitment (15+ statutes)

rules.verbatim_quote: Contractors and subcontractors at any tier are required to use a “skilled and trained workforce” to complete a contract or project if required by a statute or regulation, or if an awarding body elects to make it a requirement for a particular project.
rules.notes: DIR STW chart lists the STW statutes: https://www.dir.ca.gov/Public-Works/ADA-Compliant-STW-Chart-without-New-PRC-Provision.pdf

rules.title: STW: every worker in an apprenticeable craft must be a registered apprentice or skilled journeyperson
rules.plain_english: On STW projects, all workers in apprenticeable building trades (programs approved before Jan 1, 2014) must be either DAS-registered apprentices or 'skilled journeypersons' - graduates of an approved apprenticeship program or workers with at least as many on-the-job hours as needed to graduate.

skilled_journeyperson: graduate of CA DAS-approved or out-of-state federally approved program
OJT hours >= hours needed to graduate DAS program
parameters.occupations_covered: apprenticeable occupations with DAS-approved program before 2014-01-01

rules.verbatim_quote: “Skilled journeypersons,” meaning the worker, in the applicable occupation, either (i) graduated from an in-state, DAS-approved apprenticeship program, or an out-of-state federally-approved apprenticeship program, or (ii) has at least as many hours of on-the-job experience as would be required to graduate from the applicable DAS-approved apprenticeship program.

rules.title: STW minimum graduation requirement: 60% (30% for listed trades; teamsters exempt)
rules.plain_english: At least 60% of skilled journeypersons in each apprenticeable occupation (per contractor, per month) must be apprenticeship graduates; the requirement stays at 30% for acoustical installers, bricklayers, carpenters, cement masons, drywall/lathers, marble masons, modular furniture installers, operating engineers, pile drivers, plasterers, roofers/waterproofers, stone masons, surveyors, terrazzo workers and tile setters; teamsters are excluded. Measure by headcount or hours.

parameters.calc_unit: each contractor/subcontractor, each occupation, each calendar month
calc_methods: % of skilled journeypersons who are graduates
% of skilled-journeyperson hours worked by graduates

rules.verbatim_quote: The Minimum Graduation Requirements are fixed at 30% for: acoustical installers, bricklayers, carpenters, cement masons, drywall installers or lathers, marble masons, finishers, or setters, modular furniture or systems installers, operating engineers, pile drivers, plasterers, roofers or waterproofers, stone masons, surveyors, terrazzo workers or finishers, and tile layers, setters, and finishers.
rules.notes: Workforces may not be combined across subcontractors. Partial exemption for occupations with no DAS program before 1995 (up to half via pre-program journeypersons).

rules.title: STW graduation % does not apply when under 10 hours per month in a craft
rules.plain_english: A contractor is exempt from the graduation percentage for a month and occupation if its skilled journeypersons in that craft work fewer than 10 hours total on the project that month; other STW rules still apply.

parameters.period: calendar month covered by Monthly Compliance Report

rules.verbatim_quote: A contractor or subcontractor is exempt from the Minimum Percentage Graduation Requirements if, during the calendar month covered by the Monthly Compliance Report, the contractor or subcontractor employs skilled journeypersons who, in total, perform fewer than 10 hours of work in a particular craft on the contract or project.
rules.notes: Example: 9 carpenters x 1 hr = 9 hrs exempt; 4 roofers x 3 hrs = 12 hrs not exempt.

rules.title: STW graduation % exemption for small unlisted subs (<= 0.5% of prime contract)
rules.plain_english: A subcontractor is exempt from the graduation percentage while it is not a listed (or substitute-for-listed) subcontractor under PCC 4104 and its subcontract does not exceed one-half of one percent of the prime contract price.
rules.verbatim_quote: A subcontractor is exempt from meeting the Minimum Graduation Requirements if it meets both of the following: (i) the subcontractor was not a listed subcontractor under Public Contract Code section 4104 or a substitute for a listed subcontractor, and (ii) the subcontract does not exceed one-half of one percent of the price of the prime contract.

rules.title: STW Monthly Compliance Report to the awarding body
rules.plain_english: The prime must give the awarding body a Monthly Compliance Report for each month of work showing that it and all subs at every tier met STW requirements; subs must give the prime complete information. Each report covers a calendar month from the start date (e.g., Sept 7 - Oct 7).

parameters.covers: contractor and all subcontractors at every tier
parameters.sub_duty: submit complete STW info to contractor

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors on STW projects
rules.verbatim_quote: The contractor, bidder, or other entity must submit a Monthly Compliance Report to the public entity on a monthly basis for each month while the STW-covered project or contract is being performed. The report covers a calendar month.
rules.notes: Enforceable agreement must commit to PCC 2600-2603 compliance and monthly reports.

rules.title: STW noncompliance: awarding body withholds 150% of monthly billing
rules.plain_english: If a Monthly Compliance Report shows noncompliance, the awarding body withholds 150% of the monthly billing of the noncompliant contractor or sub (all payments if no/incomplete report from the prime); the prime may withhold the same from the offending sub. Payments resume upon a complete report, substitution of the sub with an STW-committed sub, or a Substantial Compliance Plan.

resume_when: offending sub substituted under PCC 4100-4114 with STW commitment
Substantial Compliance Plan submitted (unless timely rejected)

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors on STW projects
rules.verbatim_quote: Withhold further payments in an amount equal to (1) 150 percent of the value of the monthly billing for the contractor, bidder, or entity that failed to comply with the STW requirements of Public Contract Code sections 2600 – 2603, or (2) 150 percent of the value of the monthly billing for the subcontractor that failed to comply
rules.notes: Awarding body forwards noncompliant reports to the Labor Commissioner.

rules.title: STW penalties: up to $5,000/month ($10,000 repeat); debarment up to 3 years
rules.plain_english: STW violations carry civil penalties of up to $5,000 per month of noncompliant work, or up to $10,000 per month for a second or later violation within 3 years; fraud or two willful violations in 3 years can lead to debarment up to 3 years.

debarment_triggers: two or more willful violations within 3 years

rules.verbatim_quote: The Labor Commissioner can issue a civil penalty of up to $5,000 per month for work performed in violation of Public Contract Code Section 2600-2603. A contractor or subcontractor that commits a second or subsequent violation within a three-year period, may be assessed a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per month.
rules.notes: Penalty factors include whether a Substantial Compliance Plan was submitted and followed.

rules.title: STW prime safe harbor: include PCC 2600-2603 in subcontracts, monitor, withhold, get declaration
rules.plain_english: A prime avoids liability for a sub's STW penalties only if it: includes a copy of PCC 2600-2603 in the subcontract, periodically monitors the sub's workforce, takes corrective action including retaining 150% of amounts due, and obtains the sub's declaration under penalty of perjury of STW compliance before final payment (and lacked knowledge of the violation).

parameters.subcontract_must_include: copy of Public Contract Code 2600-2603 (Ch. 2.9, Pt. 1, Div. 2)
parameters.declaration_before_final_payment: under penalty of perjury that sub met PCC 2600-2603

rules.verbatim_quote: Include a copy of Chapter 2.9 of Part 1 of Division 2 of the Public Contract Code (sections 2600 - 2603) in contracts executed after January 1, 2019, between the contractor and the subcontractor for work on the STW-covered project;

rules.title: Subcontractor listing: subs over 1/2 of 1% of the bid (streets/highways: greater of 1/2% or $10,000)
rules.plain_english: In a public works bid, the prime must list every subcontractor who will perform work worth more than one-half of 1% of the prime's total bid. For street, highway and bridge bids, list subs over the greater of one-half of 1% or $10,000.

includes: licensed subs who specially fabricate and install per detailed drawings
parameters.formula: list if sub_amount > max(0.005*total_bid, 10000 if streets_highways else 0)

rules.verbatim_quote: in an amount in excess of one-half of 1 percent of the prime contractor’s total bid or, in the case of bids or offers for the construction of streets or highways, including bridges, in excess of one-half of 1 percent of the prime contractor’s total bid or ten thousand dollars ($10,000), whichever is greater.

rules.title: What the subcontractor list must show
rules.plain_english: For each listed sub: name, location of place of business, California contractor license number, DIR public works contractor registration number, and the portion of work it will do. List only one sub for each portion of work.
rules.verbatim_quote: (b) The portion of the work that will be done by each subcontractor under this act. The prime contractor shall list only one subcontractor for each portion as is defined by the prime contractor in his or her bid.

rules.title: 24-hour fixes after bid opening for listing errors and extra sub info
rules.plain_english: An inadvertent error in a listed sub's license or DIR registration number is not grounds for protest if the corrected number (matching the listed name and location) is submitted within 24 hours after bid opening. Agencies may also allow other requested sub information (beyond name, location, license and registration numbers) up to 24 hours after the bid deadline.
rules.verbatim_quote: (2) An inadvertent error in listing the California contractor license number or public works contractor registration number provided pursuant to paragraph (1) shall not be grounds for filing a bid protest or grounds for considering the bid nonresponsive if the corrected contractor’s license number is submitted to the public entity by the prime contractor within 24 hours after the bid opening
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Unlisted work over 1/2% must be self-performed
rules.plain_english: If the prime doesn't list a sub (or lists more than one) for a portion of work over one-half of 1% of its bid, it is deemed fully qualified and must perform that portion itself; subcontracting it later (except under 4107/4109) triggers 4111 penalties.
rules.verbatim_quote: If a prime contractor fails to specify a subcontractor or if a prime contractor specifies more than one subcontractor for the same portion of work to be performed under the contract in excess of one–half of 1 percent of the prime contractor’s total bid, the prime contractor agrees that he or she is fully qualified to perform that portion himself or herself,
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Allowed grounds to substitute a listed subcontractor
rules.plain_english: After award, a listed sub may be replaced only with the awarding authority's consent for: refusal to sign a subcontract at its bid price/scope; insolvency or bankruptcy; failure/refusal to perform; failure to provide required bonds; inadvertent clerical listing error; no license; substantially unsatisfactory work or delay; debarment under LC 1777.1/1777.7; or not a responsible contractor. Assignment or unauthorized performance by others is also barred.

grounds: fails/refuses to execute written subcontract at bid scope/price
insolvent or bankruptcy order for relief
work substantially unsatisfactory or substantially delaying/disrupting

rules.verbatim_quote: (a) Substitute a person as subcontractor in place of the subcontractor listed in the original bid, except that the awarding authority, or its duly authorized officer, may, except as otherwise provided in Section 4107.5, consent to the substitution of another person as a subcontractor in any of the following situations:
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Also STW noncompliance can be cured by substitution under 4100-4114.

rules.title: Substitution procedure: notice to listed sub, 5 working days to object, hearing
rules.plain_english: Before approving a substitution, the awarding authority must notify the listed sub in writing by certified or registered mail of the request and reasons. The sub has 5 working days to object in writing (silence = consent); if it objects, the authority gives at least 5 working days' notice of a hearing.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors, listed subs, awarding bodies
rules.verbatim_quote: The listed subcontractor who has been so notified has five working days within which to submit written objections to the substitution to the awarding authority. Failure to file these written objections constitutes the listed subcontractor’s consent to the substitution.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Clerical listing error: notice within 2 working days; objections 6; affidavits 8
rules.plain_english: To claim an inadvertent clerical error in listing a sub, the prime must give written notice to the awarding authority, the wrongly listed sub and the intended sub within 2 working days after bid opening. The listed sub has 6 working days from bid opening to object; affidavits from the parties are due within 8 working days.
rules.verbatim_quote: The prime contractor as a condition to assert a claim of inadvertent clerical error in the listing of a subcontractor shall within two working days after the time of the prime bid opening by the awarding authority give written notice to the awarding authority and copies of that notice to both the subcontractor he or she claims to have listed in error and the intended subcontractor
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: No subletting unlisted portions over 1/2% (except change orders or emergencies)
rules.plain_english: Other than for change orders, a prime may not sublet any portion of work over one-half of 1% of its total bid for which no sub was listed; subletting such work is allowed only in a public emergency or necessity with a written public finding. Listed subcontracts may not be assigned or performed by others without consent.
rules.verbatim_quote: (c) Other than in the performance of “change orders” causing changes or deviations from the original contract, sublet or subcontract any portion of the work in excess of one-half of 1 percent of the prime contractor’s total bid as to which his or her original bid did not designate a subcontractor.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. PCC 4105: listing a contractor who then sublets the majority of the work is circumvention subject to 4110/4111 penalties.

rules.title: Prime may require sub bonds only if specified in the sub-bid request
rules.plain_english: A prime may require a subcontractor's performance and payment bond (from an admitted surety, prime as obligee, at the prime's expense at the standard premium) only if its written or published request for sub-bids clearly states the bond amount and requirements - and whether the sub pays. If the sub then fails to provide it, the prime may reject and substitute.

parameters.sub_fails_to_provide: prime may reject and substitute under 4107

rules.verbatim_quote: (c)(1) The bond or bonds may be required under this section only if the prime contractor in his or her written or published request for subbids clearly specifies the amount and requirements of the bond or bonds.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. PCC 7201(b)(2) ties sub retention cap exceptions to 4108(c) bond notice.

rules.title: Subletting Act violations: contract cancellation or penalty up to 10% of subcontract; CSLB discipline
rules.plain_english: A prime that violates the Subletting and Subcontracting Fair Practices Act breaches its contract; the awarding authority may cancel the contract or assess a penalty up to 10% of the subcontract involved (after a public hearing with 5 days' notice). It is also grounds for CSLB discipline.

rules.verbatim_quote: the awarding authority may exercise the option, in its own discretion, of (1) canceling his or her contract or (2) assessing the prime contractor a penalty in an amount of not more than 10 percent of the amount of the subcontract involved, and this penalty shall be deposited in the fund out of which the prime contract is awarded.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. 2026 Law Book p.351: B&P 7110 lists willful violation of the Subletting Act (PCC 4100 et seq.) as cause for discipline.

rules.title: Late material addenda extend bid closing by at least 72 hours
rules.plain_english: If the agency issues material changes to the bid invitation later than 72 hours before bid closing, the bid deadline must be extended by at least 72 hours. Late bids are returned unopened.

parameters.material_change: substantial cost impact on total bid

rules.verbatim_quote: The date and time shall be extended by no less than 72 hours if the officer, department, board, or commission issues any material changes, additions, or deletions to the invitation later than 72 hours prior to the bid closing. Any bids received after the time specified in the notice or any extension due to material changes shall be returned unopened.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Noncollusion declaration required with every public works bid
rules.plain_english: Every bid on a public entity's public works contract must include a noncollusion declaration signed under penalty of perjury in the statutory form, stating the bid is genuine and not collusive, with the signer's title, date, city and state.

parameters.required_with: every bid on every public works contract of a public entity
parameters.form_title: NONCOLLUSION DECLARATION TO BE EXECUTED BY BIDDER AND SUBMITTED WITH BID

rules.verbatim_quote: The bid is not made in the interest of, or on behalf of, any undisclosed person, partnership, company, association, organization, or corporation. The bid is genuine and not collusive or sham. The bidder has not directly or indirectly induced or solicited any other bidder to put in a false or sham bid.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Full statutory form text is on PDF pages 1164-1165 - a tool can generate it verbatim.

rules.title: Bid security on state contracts: at least 10% of the bid
rules.plain_english: Bids on State Contract Act projects must be sealed and include bidder's security of at least 10% of the bid: an admitted surety bid bond (signed or electronic via approved registry), cash, cashier's check or certified check payable to the department director. Bids without security are not considered.

forms: electronic bid bond by admitted surety via approved registry
signed bid bond by admitted surety

rules.applies_to: Bidders on state agency public works
rules.verbatim_quote: (b) The required bidder’s security shall be in an amount equal to at least 10 percent of the amount bid. A bid shall not be considered unless one of the forms of bidder’s security is enclosed with it.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Bid security is forfeited if the low bidder fails to execute the contract, including for lack of proper license (PCC 10164).

rules.title: Bid security on local agency contracts (commonly 10%)
rules.plain_english: Cities, counties, special districts and school districts generally require bid security (bid bond, cash or check); several city/district statutes set it at 10% of the bid, and school districts set it in the bid documents (commonly 10%). Check each solicitation.
rules.applies_to: Bidders on local agency public works
rules.source_location: Secondary search snippets (leginfo unreachable); e.g., california.public.law and district bidding guides
rules.notes: Figures from search-engine excerpts only. Bid documents control the required amount and form; verify the statute for each agency type.

rules.title: CSLB license required to bid public works; unlicensed bids rejected, contracts void
rules.plain_english: Submitting a bid to a public agency without a contractor's license is a misdemeanor (with limited exceptions). Unlicensed bids are nonresponsive and must be rejected; local agencies must verify the license before award; contracts with unlicensed contractors are void. Repeat offenders face a fine of the greater of 20% of the contract price or $4,500, and/or 10 days to 6 months in jail.
rules.applies_to: All bidders on public agency contracts
rules.source_location: PDF pages 252-253 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: (e) Unless one of the foregoing exceptions applies, a bid submitted to a public agency by a contractor who is not licensed in accordance with this chapter shall be considered nonresponsive and shall be rejected by the public agency.
rules.notes: Same section: 'Any contract awarded to, or any purchase order issued to, a contractor who is not licensed pursuant to this chapter is void.'

rules.title: Federal-aid state projects: bid OK without CA license, but must be licensed at award
rules.plain_english: On state projects involving federal funds, a bid isn't invalid because the bidder lacks a California license, but the contractor must be properly licensed in the right classification when the contract is awarded, or it forfeits its bid security.

parameters.failure_consequence: treated as failure to execute contract; forfeiture of bidder's security

rules.applies_to: Bidders on federally funded state projects
rules.verbatim_quote: In all state projects where federal funds are involved, no bid submitted shall be invalidated by the failure of the bidder to be licensed in accordance with the laws of this state. However, at the time the contract is awarded, the contractor shall be properly licensed in accordance with the laws of this state.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. PCC 20103.5 (local agencies) text exists in the 2022 appendix p.1173 but was not separately excerpted here.

rules.title: Licensees may bid jointly before getting a joint venture license
rules.plain_english: Two or more licensed contractors may submit a joint bid before obtaining a joint venture license, but must have the joint venture license before being awarded the contract and acting jointly; failure to get it doesn't excuse bid-default penalties.
rules.source_location: PDF page 255 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: (b) Prior to obtaining a joint venture license, contractors licensed in accordance with this chapter may jointly bid for the performance of work covered by this section.

rules.title: Public works: awarding authority sets required license class; specialty prime must hold majority class
rules.plain_english: The awarding authority determines the license classification needed to bid and perform a public works project using CSLB's classifications. A specialty contractor may not get the prime contract unless its classification covers a majority of the project, and work outside its specialty (other than incidental and supplemental work) must go to licensed subs per the Subletting Act.

parameters.classification_set_by: awarding authority using CSLB regs (16 CCR Div. 8)
parameters.outside_specialty_work: licensed subcontractor per PCC 4100 et seq.

rules.applies_to: Specialty and general contractors bidding public works
rules.source_location: PDF page 278 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: In no case shall the awarding authority award a prime contract to a specialty contractor whose classification constitutes less than a majority of the project.
rules.notes: Amended by SB 1455 (Stats 2024 ch 485) eff. 1/1/2025; CSLB Summer 2026 newsletter confirms agencies must use CSLB classification descriptions.

rules.title: State agencies verify license classification before award (every 2 years)
rules.plain_english: Before awarding a contract, a state agency must verify with CSLB that the contractor holds a classification appropriate to the work (once every two years per contractor), or accept the pocket license plus a sworn statement that it is current, valid and in the right classification.

parameters.alternative: pocket license/certificate + statement under penalty of perjury

rules.verbatim_quote: (a) A state agency, as defined in Section 10335.7 that is subject to this code, shall, prior to awarding a contract for work to be performed by a contractor, as defined by Section 7026 of the Business and Professions Code, verify with the Contractors State License Board that the person seeking the contract is licensed in a classification appropriate to the work to be undertaken.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Public contract delay damages unenforceable unless liquidated
rules.plain_english: In public works contracts entered on or after Jan 1, 2016 (not state departments under PCC 10106), a clause making the contractor liable for delay damages is unenforceable unless the damages are liquidated to a set amount stated in the contract; no delay damages after notice of completion/acceptance.

parameters.must_be: liquidated to a set amount and identified in contract

rules.verbatim_quote: (a) A public works contract entered into on or after January 1, 2016, that contains a clause that expressly requires a contractor to be responsible for delay damages is not enforceable unless the delay damages have been liquidated to a set amount and identified in the public works contract.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: State contracts: pay subs within 7 days of each progress payment (PCC 10262)
rules.plain_english: On state agency contracts, the prime must pay each subcontractor its share within seven days after receiving each progress payment; diversion is grounds for action and CSLB discipline, and subs must notify CSLB and the department in writing of underpayments.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors on state agency contracts
rules.source_location: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf PDF page 1172 (Appendix, PCC §10262); PDF page 349 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (B&P §7108.5(e))
rules.verbatim_quote: The contractor shall pay to his or her subcontractors, within seven days of receipt of each progress payment, the respective amounts allowed the contractor on account of the work performed by his or her subcontractors, to the extent of each subcontractor’s interest therein.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Overlaps lien/payment research (bp-7108-5-pay-subs-7-days). B&P 7108.5 applies to all public works 'except where Section 10262 of the Public Contract Code applies.'

rules.title: Payment bond required on public works over $25,000
rules.plain_english: A direct contractor awarded a public works contract over $25,000 must furnish a payment bond (reportedly at least 100% of the contract) before starting work; the agency's bid call must say a payment bond is required, and the agency cannot pay the contractor's claims if no approved bond is given.

parameters.no_bond_consequence: public entity may not pay contractor's claims (CC 9552)

rules.source_location: Secondary: search-engine excerpts of leginfo/Justia text (leginfo unreachable)
rules.notes: Overlaps lien/payment research rules public-payment-bond-required-25000 and public-payment-bond-amount-100pct (also unverified). State-entity contracts under PCC 7103 have their own bond rules. The 2026 CSLB Law Book (PDF page 42) only describes bonds generally.

rules.title: Performance vs. payment bonds and typical cost (1-2%)
rules.plain_english: A performance bond guarantees the project gets completed per plans and specs; a payment bond assures labor and material claimants get paid. Bonds typically cost about 1-2% of the contract price - include this cost in bids.

parameters.payment_bond: assures payment of labor and material claims
parameters.surety_max_liability: face amount unless surety takes over completion

rules.citation: CSLB Law Book Ch. 3 (Managing a Business) - Bonds
rules.source_location: PDF page 42 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: Bonds can be obtained from bonding companies for a percentage of the contract price, usually in the one to two percent range. This requirement is the cost of doing business that should be recognized when the bid is submitted.
rules.notes: Educational text, not statute. Performance bond amounts/thresholds are set by agency statute or bid documents (not verified here).

rules.title: Government bids may require DVBE/minority/women business participation steps
rules.plain_english: Federal, state and local agencies, utilities and some private owners may require bidders to take specific steps to meet minority, women and disabled veteran business enterprise (DVBE) goals; check the solicitation and DGS's Office of Small Business and DVBE Services.

parameters.contact: DGS Procurement Division, Office of Small Business and DVBE Services (OSDS), (916) 376-5000, OSDSHelp@dgs.ca.gov

rules.citation: CSLB Law Book Ch. 3 - Bidding on Government Contracts
rules.source_location: PDF page 82 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: Contractors bidding in California should know that there are a variety of federal, state, and local governmental agencies, as well as public utilities and private corporations, which may require a bidder to take specific steps to achieve established minority, women, and disabled veteran business enterprise (DVBE) goals.
rules.notes: Educational text in the official law book.

rules.title: State contracting goals: 3% DVBE participation, 25% small business
rules.plain_english: State agencies must aim to award at least 3% of annual contract dollars to certified DVBEs and at least 25% to certified small businesses (including microbusinesses); state solicitations often include a DVBE participation requirement or incentive that bidders must meet or document good-faith efforts for.

parameters.solicitation_specific_goal: may be above or below 3% (2 CCR 1896.70, reported)

rules.citation: Military & Veterans Code 999 et seq.; Public Contract Code 10115; Government Code 14838
rules.source_location: Secondary: search-engine summaries of DGS, LAO and code reprints (dgs.ca.gov, lao.ca.gov not reachable)
rules.notes: Not read from primary text. Certification through DGS OSDS. Verify the solicitation's DVBE requirement, incentive and documentation (e.g., DVBE declarations) per bid.
